title.en: Volume 15: Shancheng's (Tuoba Shiyijian) Children and Grandchildren
title.raw: 卷15 昭成子孫 Volume 15: Shancheng's (Tuoba Shiyijian) Children and Grandchildren

sentences.zh: 寔君者，昭成皇帝之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Lord Shi was the eldest son by a concubine of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi, born to a concubine, was Emperor Zhaocheng's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性愚戇，安忍不仁。

translations.literal: By nature dull and obstinate, he endured cruelty and lacked benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: He was slow-witted and stubborn, cruel by nature and devoid of mercy.

sentences.zh: 昭成季年，苻堅遣其行唐公苻洛等來寇南境，昭成遣劉庫仁逆戰於石子嶺。

translations.literal: In the late years of Zhaocheng, Fu Jian sent his Xingtang Duke Fu Luo and others to raid the southern border; Zhaocheng sent Liu Kuren to meet them in battle at Shizi Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhaocheng's reign Fu Jian sent Fu Luo, Duke of Xingtang, and others against the southern marches; Zhaocheng dispatched Liu Kuren to fight them at Shizi Ridge.

sentences.zh: 昭成時不勝，不能親勒眾軍，乃率諸部避難陰山，度漠北。

translations.literal: At that time Zhaocheng did not prevail and could not personally lead the host in person; he then led the tribes to take refuge in the Yin Mountains and crossed north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng was losing and too weak to command the army himself, so he led the tribes into the Yin Mountains and beyond the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 高車四面寇抄，復度漠南。

translations.literal: The Gaoche raided on all sides; he again crossed south of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche bands harried them from every quarter, forcing him back south of the desert.

sentences.zh: 苻洛軍退，乃還雲中。

translations.literal: When Fu Luo's army withdrew, he then returned to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu Luo retreated he returned to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 初，昭成以弟孤讓國，乃以半部授孤。

translations.literal: At first Zhaocheng, because his younger brother Gu yielded the state, gave half the tribes to Gu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhaocheng had ceded half the realm to his brother Gu when Gu renounced the throne.

sentences.zh: 孤卒，子斤失職懷怨，欲伺隙為亂。

translations.literal: When Gu died, his son Jin lost his post and nursed resentment, wishing to watch for an opening to make trouble.
translations.idiomatic: After Gu's death his son Jin, stripped of office, brooded on revenge and waited for a chance to rebel.

sentences.zh: 是時，獻明皇帝及秦明王翰皆先終，太祖年六歲，昭成不豫，慕容后子閼婆等雖長，而國統未定。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xianming and Prince Qinming Han had both died first; Taizu was six years old; Zhaocheng was ill; and though Murong the empress's sons Yueba and others were older, the succession was unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianming and Prince Qinming Han were already dead; Taizu was only six; Zhaocheng lay ill; and though Yueba and other sons of Empress Murong were grown, no heir had been chosen.

sentences.zh: 斤因是說寔君曰：「帝將立慕容所生，而懼汝為變，欲先殺汝，是以頃日以來，諸子戎服，夜持兵仗，遶汝廬舍，伺便將發，吾愍而相告。

translations.literal: Jin thereupon persuaded Lord Shi, saying: "The emperor intends to install the son born of Murong and fears you will make trouble; he wishes to kill you first. That is why in recent days the princes have worn armor, held weapons by night, and circled your lodge waiting for a chance to strike. I pity you and tell you."
translations.idiomatic: Jin then told Lord Shi: "The emperor means to put Murong's son on the throne and, fearing you will rebel, plans to kill you first. That is why the princes have lately gone about in armor at night with weapons in hand, circling your quarters for a chance to strike. Out of pity I warn you."

sentences.zh: 」時苻洛等軍猶在君子津，夜常警備，諸皇子挾仗徬徨廬舍之間。

translations.literal: At that time Fu Luo's army was still at Junzi Ford; by night they were always on alert; the princes wandered among the lodges clutching weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Luo's troops still held Junzi Ford and stood watch through the nights, while the princes paced the lodges armed.

sentences.zh: 寔君視察，以斤言為信，乃率其屬盡害諸皇子，昭成亦暴崩。

translations.literal: Lord Shi inspected and believed Jin's words; he then led his followers and killed all the princes; Zhaocheng also died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi looked about, took Jin at his word, and with his men slaughtered every prince; Zhaocheng died the same night.

sentences.zh: 其夜，諸皇子婦及宮人奔告苻洛軍，堅將李柔、張蚝勒兵內逼，部眾離散。

translations.literal: That night the princes' wives and palace women ran to report to Fu Luo's army; Fu Jian's generals Li Rou and Zhang Hao led troops inward in pressure, and the tribes scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That night the princes' wives and palace women fled to Fu Luo's camp; Fu Jian's generals Li Rou and Zhang Hao pressed inward with troops and the tribes broke apart.

sentences.zh: 苻堅聞之，召燕鳳問其故，以狀對。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian heard of it he summoned Yan Feng and asked the reason; he answered with the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian, hearing the news, summoned Yan Feng and asked what had happened; Yan Feng told him the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 堅曰：「天下之惡一也。

translations.literal: Fu Jian said: "Evil under heaven is one."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian said, "There is only one kind of evil in the world."

sentences.zh: 」乃執寔君及斤，轘之於長安西市。

translations.literal: He then seized Lord Shi and Jin and had them torn apart at the West Market of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Lord Shi and Jin and had them dismembered at Chang'an's West Market.

sentences.zh: 寔君孫勿期，位定州刺史，賜爵林慮侯。

translations.literal: Lord Shi's grandson Wuqi held the post of Inspector of Dingzhou and was granted the title Marquis of Linlu.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Shi's grandson Wuqi served as Inspector of Dingzhou and was enfeoffed Marquis of Linlu.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away.

sentences.zh: 子六狀，真定侯。

translations.literal: His son Liuzhuang was Marquis of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liuzhuang held the title Marquis of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 子儀，長七尺五寸，容貌甚偉，美鬚髯，有算略，少能舞劍，騎射絕人。

translations.literal: His son Yi was seven feet five inches tall, of very imposing appearance, with a fine beard; he had stratagems; in youth he could dance with the sword; in mounted archery he had no peer.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi stood seven feet five, strikingly handsome with a splendid beard; clever in counsel, he danced with the sword as a youth and was unmatched in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 太祖幸賀蘭部，侍從出入。

translations.literal: When Taizu visited the Helan tribe, Yi attended him in and out.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu visited the Helan, Yi attended him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 登國初，賜爵九原公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he was granted the title Duke of Jiuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dengguo era he was made Duke of Jiuyuan.

sentences.zh: 從破諸部，有謀戰功。

translations.literal: He followed in breaking the tribes and had merit in planning and battle.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned in the subjugation of the tribes and won distinction both in counsel and in the field.

sentences.zh: 及太祖將圖慕容垂，遣儀觀釁。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to scheme against Murong Chui, he sent Yi to probe for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu prepared to move against Murong Chui he sent Yi to test the enemy.

sentences.zh: 垂問儀太祖不自來之意，儀曰：「先人以來，世據北土，子孫相承，不失其舊。

translations.literal: Chui asked Yi the meaning of Taizu not coming in person; Yi said: "From our forebears down, we have held the northern lands generation after generation, and our descendants have succeeded without losing the old order.
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked why Taizu had not come himself; Yi replied: "Since our ancestors' time we have held the north, generation after generation, without forfeiting our heritage.

sentences.zh: 乃祖受晉正朔，[3]爵稱代王，東與燕世為兄弟。

translations.literal: Our founding ancestor received the Jin calendar,[3] was enfeoffed as King of Dai, and eastward we and Yan have been brothers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Our founder accepted investiture under the Jin calendar,[3] took the title King of Dai, and for generations Yan and we have stood as brothers in the east.

sentences.zh: 儀之奉命，理謂非失。

translations.literal: That Yi should come on command is, by reason, no fault."
translations.idiomatic: My coming on orders is, by rights, no lapse."

sentences.zh: 」垂壯其對，因戲曰：「吾威加四海，卿主不自見吾，云何非失？

translations.literal: Chui admired his reply and jested, saying: "My might fills the four seas; your lord will not come to see me—how is that not a fault?"
translations.idiomatic: Chui admired the answer and said in jest, "My power spans the seas—yet your master will not come to see me. How is that no fault?"

sentences.zh: 」儀曰：「燕若不修文德，欲以兵威自強，此乃本朝將帥之事，非儀所知也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "If Yan will not cultivate civil virtue and wishes to strengthen itself by military might, that is the business of our commanders; it is not for Yi to know."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "If Yan neglects civil virtue and trusts only to arms, that is a matter for our generals, not for me to judge."

sentences.zh: 」及還，報曰：「垂死乃可圖，今則未可。

translations.literal: When he returned he reported: "Chui may be taken only when he is dying; not yet."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported, "Chui can be struck only when he is near death—not yet."

sentences.zh: 」太祖作色問之。

translations.literal: Taizu changed color and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's face darkened and he pressed him for an explanation.

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「垂年已暮，其子寶弱而無威，謀不能決。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Chui is already old; his son Bao is weak and without authority; in counsel he cannot decide.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Chui is old; his son Bao is feeble and commands no awe; he cannot settle on a plan.

sentences.zh: 慕容德自負才氣，非弱主之臣。

translations.literal: Murong De trusts in his own talent and is no minister for a weak master.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De is proud of his gifts and will not serve a feeble lord.

sentences.zh: 釁將內起，是可計之。

translations.literal: A breach will rise within; he may be taken by design."
translations.idiomatic: Strife will break out within their house—then they can be taken."

sentences.zh: 」太祖以為然。

translations.literal: Taizu thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 後改封平原公。

translations.literal: Later his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reassigned as Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖征衞辰，儀出別道，獲衞辰尸，傳首行宮。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Wei Chen, Yi marched by a separate route, obtained Wei Chen's corpse, and sent the head to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu's campaign against Wei Chen, Yi took a separate road, seized Wei Chen's body, and sent the head to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太祖大喜，徙封東平公。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased and transferred his enfeoffment to Duke of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was delighted and raised him to Duke of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 命督屯田於河北，自五原至棝楊塞外，分農稼，大得人心。

translations.literal: He was ordered to supervise garrison farming in Hebei, from Wuyuan to beyond Yusang Pass, dividing the crops; he won great popular regard.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to oversee garrison agriculture in Hebei from Wuyuan to beyond Yusang Pass, apportioning the harvests, and won deep loyalty among the people.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶之寇五原，儀攝據朔方，要其還路。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao raided Wuyuan, Yi held Shuofang in his stead and blocked Bao's line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao struck at Wuyuan, Yi held Shuofang and barred his retreat.

sentences.zh: 及并州平，儀功多，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: When Bingzhou was pacified, Yi's merit was great and he was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Bingzhou was pacified his service stood foremost and he was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 從圍中山。

translations.literal: He followed in the siege of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the siege of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 慕容德之敗也，太祖以普驎妻周氏賜儀，并其僮僕財物。

translations.literal: When Murong De was defeated, Taizu gave Yi Murong Pulong's wife Lady Zhou, together with her servants and goods.
translations.idiomatic: After Murong De's defeat Taizu gave Yi Lady Zhou, Murong Pulong's wife, with her household and possessions.

sentences.zh: 尋遷都督中外諸軍事、左丞相，進封衞王。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without and Left Chancellor, and advanced to Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without and Left Chancellor, and was raised to Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 中山平，復遣儀討鄴，平之。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified, Yi was again sent to attack Ye and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he was sent again to take Ye and subdued it.

sentences.zh: 太祖將還代都，置中山行臺，詔儀守尚書令以鎮之，遠近懷附。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to return to the Dai capital, he set up a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan, ordered Yi to remain Director of the Masters of Writing to guard it, and near and far submitted in trust.
translations.idiomatic: As Taizu prepared to return to the Dai capital he established a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan and left Yi as Director of the Masters of Writing to hold the city; the region submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 尋徵儀以丞相入輔。

translations.literal: Soon Yi was summoned to enter court as chancellor to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was soon recalled to serve at court as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 又從征高車。

translations.literal: He again followed on the campaign against the Gaoche.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned again against the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 儀別從西北破其別部。

translations.literal: Yi separately marched from the northwest and broke their detached division.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took a separate route from the northwest and shattered a detached Gaoche force.

sentences.zh: 又從討姚平，有功，賜以絹布綿牛馬羊等。

translations.literal: He again followed in attacking Yao Ping and had merit; he was granted silk, cloth, cotton, cattle, horses, sheep, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the attack on Yao Ping and was rewarded with silk, cloth, cotton, cattle, horses, sheep, and the like.

sentences.zh: 儀膂力過人，弓力將十石；

translations.literal: Yi's bodily strength surpassed others; his bow drew nearly ten stone;
translations.idiomatic: Yi's strength was extraordinary; his bow drew nearly ten stone;

sentences.zh: 陳留公虔，矟大稱異。

translations.literal: Duke of Chenliu Qian's spear was greatly praised as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: and Duke of Chenliu Qian's spear was famed as matchless.

sentences.zh: 時人云：「衞王弓，桓王矟。」

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Prince of Wei's bow, Prince Huan's spear."
translations.idiomatic: Men said at the time, "Prince of Wei's bow, Prince Huan's spear."

sentences.zh: 世祖之初育也，太祖喜，夜召儀入。

translations.literal: When Shizu was first born, Taizu rejoiced and summoned Yi at night.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was born Taizu rejoiced and called Yi to him at night.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「卿聞夜喚，乃不怪懼乎？

translations.literal: Taizu said: "When you heard a night summons, were you not startled and afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizu asked, "When you were summoned at night, were you not afraid?"

sentences.zh: 」儀曰：「臣推誠以事陛下，陛下明察，臣輒自安。

translations.literal: Yi said: "Your servant serves Your Majesty with full loyalty; Your Majesty is discerning, and your servant is always at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "I serve Your Majesty with open heart; Your Majesty sees clearly, and I am always at peace.

sentences.zh: 忽奉夜詔，怪有之，懼實無也。

translations.literal: Suddenly to receive a night edict—wonder there may be, but fear there is none."
translations.idiomatic: A sudden summons at night may surprise, but it never frightens me."

sentences.zh: 」太祖告以世祖生，儀起拜而歌舞，遂對飲申旦。

translations.literal: Taizu told him of Shizu's birth; Yi rose, bowed, and sang and danced; they then drank facing each other until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu told him of Shizu's birth; Yi rose, bowed, sang and danced for joy, and they drank together until dawn.

sentences.zh: 召羣臣入，賜儀御馬、御帶、縑錦等。

translations.literal: He summoned the ministers to enter and granted Yi the imperial horse, imperial belt, silks, and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the court and gave Yi the imperial horse, belt, silks, and brocades.

sentences.zh: 先是，上谷侯岌、張兗，代郡許謙等有名于時，學博今古，初來入國，聞儀待士，先就儀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Hou Ji of Shanggu, Zhang Gun, Xu Qian of Dai commandery, and others were famed in their time, learned in past and present; when they first entered the state they heard Yi treated scholars well and went first to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Hou Ji of Shanggu, Zhang Gun, Xu Qian of Dai, and other scholars famed for learning had come into the realm; hearing Yi honored talent, they sought him out first.

sentences.zh: 儀並禮之，共談當世之務，指畫山河，分別城邑，成敗要害，造次備舉。

translations.literal: Yi received them all with ceremony; together they discussed affairs of the age, traced rivers and mountains, distinguished cities and towns, and success and failure at key points—offhand he could set them all forth.
translations.idiomatic: Yi welcomed them all and debated the affairs of the day, mapping rivers and passes, naming cities and strongpoints, and weighing victory and defeat at every hinge—he could rehearse them all without pause.

sentences.zh: 謙等歎服，相謂曰：「平原公有大才不世之略，吾等當附其尾。」

translations.literal: Qian and the others sighed in admiration and said to one another: "The Duke of Pingyuan has great talent and a strategy not of this age; we should attach ourselves to his train."
translations.idiomatic: Qian and the rest marveled and said to one another, "The Duke of Pingyuan has genius and a strategy for the ages—we should follow in his wake."

sentences.zh: 太祖以儀器望，待之尤重，數幸其第，如家人禮。

translations.literal: Because of Yi's capacity and reputation Taizu treated him with especial weight, often visiting his residence with the courtesy due family.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu valued Yi's stature and often visited his house with the ease of kin.

sentences.zh: 儀矜功恃寵，遂與宜都公穆崇謀為亂，伏武士伺太祖，欲為逆。

translations.literal: Yi, proud of his merit and trusting in favor, then joined Duke of Yidu Mu Chong in plotting rebellion, hid armed men to wait for Taizu, and intended treason.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his deeds and secure in Taizu's favor, Yi conspired with Duke of Yidu Mu Chong, posted swordsmen to ambush Taizu, and planned treason.

sentences.zh: 崇子遂留在伏士中，太祖召之，將有所使。

translations.literal: Chong's son Suiliu remained among the hidden swordsmen; Taizu summoned him, about to give him a mission.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son Suiliu was among the hidden men when Taizu called for him on other business.

sentences.zh: 遂留聞召，恐發，踰牆告狀，太祖祕而恕之。

translations.literal: Suiliu heard the summons, feared exposure, climbed the wall to report the plot, and Taizu kept it secret and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the summons Suiliu feared discovery, scaled the wall to reveal the plot, and Taizu concealed the matter and spared him.

sentences.zh: 天賜六年，天文多變，占者云「當有逆臣伏尸流血」。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tiansi many heavenly signs changed; diviners said, "There will be a rebellious minister; corpses will lie and blood will flow."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tiansi the heavens showed many omens; diviners said a traitor would die amid slaughter.

sentences.zh: 太祖惡之，頗殺公卿，欲以厭當天災。

translations.literal: Taizu hated this and killed many ministers and dukes, wishing to appease the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu loathed the omen and executed many high officials, hoping to turn aside the calamity.

sentences.zh: 儀內不自安，單騎遁走。

translations.literal: Yi was uneasy within and fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, shaken within, fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 太祖使人追執之，遂賜死，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: Taizu sent men in pursuit to seize him and then granted him death; he was buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had him pursued, seized, and granted death; he was buried with common rites.

sentences.zh: 儀十五子。

translations.literal: Yi had fifteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yi left fifteen sons.

sentences.zh: 子纂，五歲，太祖命養於宮中。

translations.literal: His son Zuan, five years old, Taizu ordered reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan, aged five, Taizu ordered raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 少明敏，動止有禮，太祖愛之，恩與諸皇子同。

translations.literal: From youth he was bright and keen; in movement and rest he observed propriety; Taizu loved him and his favor matched the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and courteous from childhood, he won Taizu's love equal to the imperial sons.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，除定州刺史，封中山公，進爵為王，賜步挽几以優異之。

translations.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne he was appointed Inspector of Dingzhou, enfeoffed Duke of Zhongshan, advanced to prince, and granted a hand-drawn carriage and folding stool as special honors.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he became Inspector of Dingzhou, was made Duke of Zhongshan and then prince, and received a hand-drawn carriage and folding stool as marks of favor.

sentences.zh: [4]纂好酒愛佞，政以賄成，世祖殺其親嬖人。

translations.literal: [4] Zuan loved wine and favored flatterers; government was accomplished by bribes; Shizu killed his close favorites.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Zuan drank heavily and kept sycophants; office went to the highest bidder until Shizu executed his pet courtiers.

sentences.zh: 後悔過修謹，拜內大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he repented, cultivated caution, and was appointed Grand General of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He later repented, grew careful in conduct, and was made Grand General of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 居官清約簡慎，更稱廉平。

translations.literal: In office he was clear, sparing, and simple in caution; opinion again praised him as honest and fair.
translations.idiomatic: In office he lived plainly and carefully, and men again praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 纂於宗屬最長，宗室有事，咸就諮焉。

translations.literal: Zuan was eldest among the clan kindred; when the imperial house had affairs, all came to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: As the senior of the clan, he was the one the imperial kindred consulted in every family matter.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Jian.

sentences.zh: 纂弟良，性忠篤。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Liang was loyal and sincere by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's brother Liang was steadfast and true by nature.

sentences.zh: 太宗追錄儀功，封南陽王以紹儀後。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, recalling Yi's merit, enfeoffed Liang Prince of Nanyang to continue Yi's line.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, recording Yi's service, made Liang Prince of Nanyang to carry on his line.

sentences.zh: 子禎，通解諸方之語，便騎射。

translations.literal: His son Zhen understood the languages of many regions and was skilled in riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen mastered many tongues and excelled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，為司衞監。

translations.literal: In Shizu's time he was Director of the Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu he served as Director of the Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，忽遇賊別部，多少不敵，禎乃就山解鞍放馬，以示有伏，賊果疑而避之。

translations.literal: He followed on the campaign against the Rouran; suddenly they met a detached band of the enemy; they were fewer and could not match them; Zhen then went to a hill, removed saddle and let horses graze, to show there were ambush troops; the enemy indeed suspected and avoided them.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against the Rouran he suddenly met a detached band too numerous to fight; Zhen rode to a hill, slipped saddles, and loosed the horses as if an ambush lay hidden—the enemy suspected a trap and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，賜爵沛郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu he was granted the title Duke of Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozu's reign he was made Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 後拜南豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Inspector of Southern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 大胡山蠻時時鈔掠，前後守牧多羈縻而已。

translations.literal: The barbarians of Great Hu Mountain raided from time to time; former governors and protectors for the most part only held them loosely in check.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of Great Hu Mountain raided often, and earlier governors had done little more than placate them.

sentences.zh: 禎乃設畫，召新蔡、襄城蠻魁三十餘人，禎盛武裝，於州西為置酒，使之觀射。

translations.literal: Zhen then laid a plan, summoned more than thirty chieftains of the Xincai and Xiangcheng barbarians, arrayed himself in full martial dress west of the prefecture, set out wine for them, and had them watch archery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen devised a stratagem: he summoned more than thirty chiefs of the Xincai and Xiangcheng tribes, appeared west of the city in full armor, feasted them, and made them watch an archery display.

sentences.zh: 先選左右能射者二十餘人，禎自發數箭皆中，然後命左右以次而射，並中。

translations.literal: First he chose more than twenty skilled archers from his attendants; Zhen himself shot several arrows and all hit; then he ordered the attendants to shoot in turn, and all hit.
translations.idiomatic: He first chose twenty-odd expert bowmen from his guard; Zhen shot several arrows himself, every one on target, then had his men shoot in turn—all hit.

sentences.zh: 先出一囚犯死罪者，使服軍衣，亦參射限，命射不中，禎即責而斬之。

translations.literal: First he brought out a condemned prisoner and had him wear military dress and take part in the shooting as well; he ordered that if he did not hit, Zhen would rebuke and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced a condemned man in soldier's dress to shoot with the rest, with orders that Zhen would rebuke and behead him on a miss.

sentences.zh: 蠻魁等伏伎畏威，相視股慄。

translations.literal: The barbarian chieftains and others submitted in awe of his martial power, looked at one another, and their thighs trembled.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains cowered before his show of force, glancing at one another with shaking knees.

sentences.zh: 又預教左右取死囚十人，皆著蠻衣，云是鈔賊。

translations.literal: He also beforehand instructed his attendants to take ten condemned men, all dress them in barbarian clothes, and say they were raiding bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He had also secretly prepared ten condemned men dressed as raiders and passed off as bandits.

sentences.zh: 禎乃臨坐，偽舉目瞻天，微有風動，禎謂蠻曰：「風氣少暴，似有鈔賊入境，不過十人，當在西南五十里許。

translations.literal: Zhen then sat in audience, feigned to lift his eyes to heaven; there was a slight stir of wind; Zhen said to the barbarians: "The wind is somewhat violent; it seems raiding bandits have entered the border—not more than ten men, and they should be about fifty li to the southwest."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen then took his seat, pretended to scan the sky, and when a breeze stirred said to the tribesmen, "The wind runs fierce—raiders have crossed the border, no more than ten, about fifty li southwest."

sentences.zh: 」即命騎追掩，果縛送十人。

translations.literal: He at once ordered horsemen to pursue and seize them; indeed they bound and sent ten men.
translations.idiomatic: He sent horsemen at once; they returned with exactly ten bound men.

sentences.zh: 禎告諸蠻曰：「爾鄉里作賊如此，合死以不？

translations.literal: Zhen told the barbarians: "When men of your villages act as bandits like this, do they deserve death or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen asked the chiefs, "When your people raid like this, do they deserve death?"

sentences.zh: 」蠻等皆叩頭曰：「合萬死。

translations.literal: The barbarians all knocked their heads and said: "They deserve ten thousand deaths."
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed and cried, "They deserve death a thousand times over."

sentences.zh: 」禎即斬之。

translations.literal: Zhen then beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had the ten men beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 乃遣蠻還，并加慰諭。

translations.literal: He then sent the barbarians back and also added words of comfort and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the chiefs home with soothing words.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻大服，自是境無暴掠，淮南之人相率投附者三千餘家，置之城東汝水之側，名曰歸義坊。

translations.literal: The barbarians were greatly subdued; from then on within the borders there was no violent plunder; more than three thousand households of people south of the Huai came in succession to submit; they were placed on the east bank of the Ru River within the city and called the Ward of Returning Allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were thoroughly cowed; raiding ceased within his borders, and more than three thousand households south of the Huai came over; he settled them east of the city along the Ru in a quarter named Returning Allegiance.

sentences.zh: 初，豫州城豪胡丘生數與外交通。

translations.literal: At first the magnate of Yuzhou city Hu Qiusheng had several times communicated with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the city magnate Hu Qiusheng of Yuzhou had repeatedly dealt with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 及禎為刺史，丘生嘗有犯，懷恨圖為不軌，詐以婚進城人告云：「刺史欲遷城中大家，送之向代。

translations.literal: When Zhen became inspector, Qiusheng had once committed an offense; nursing hatred he plotted disloyalty and, falsely under the pretext of marriage, entered the city and told the people: "The inspector wishes to move the great households of the city and send them toward Dai."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen took office Qiusheng, smarting from an earlier offense, plotted treason; under cover of a wedding he entered the city and told the people, "The inspector means to uproot the leading families and send them to Dai."

sentences.zh: 」共謀翻城。

translations.literal: Together they plotted to turn the city.
translations.idiomatic: They conspired to seize the city.

sentences.zh: 城人石道起以事密告禎，速掩丘生并諸預謀者。

translations.literal: The townsman Shi Daoqi secretly reported the affair to Zhen; he swiftly seized Qiusheng and all who shared the plot.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman named Shi Daoqi reported the plot in secret; Zhen moved at once to seize Qiusheng and his fellow conspirators.

sentences.zh: 禎曰：「吾不負人，人何以叛，但丘生誑誤。

translations.literal: Zhen said: "I have not failed others; why should others rebel? Only Qiusheng has deceived and misled them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "I have wronged no one—why should they rebel? Only Qiusheng has misled them.

sentences.zh: 若即收掩，眾必大懼。

translations.literal: If I seize them at once the multitude will surely be greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: If I arrest them now the people will panic.

sentences.zh: 吾靜以待之，不久自當悔服。

translations.literal: I will wait quietly; before long they will themselves repent and submit."
translations.idiomatic: I will wait calmly; soon they will repent and submit of themselves."

sentences.zh: 」語未訖，而城中三百人自縛詣州門，陳丘生譎誑之罪。

translations.literal: Before the words were finished, three hundred men in the city bound themselves and came to the prefectural gate, stating Qiusheng's crime of deceit and delusion.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished speaking when three hundred townsmen came to the gate with ropes on their own backs, denouncing Qiusheng's lies.

sentences.zh: 丘生單騎逃走。

translations.literal: Qiusheng fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Qiusheng escaped on a lone horse.

sentences.zh: 禎恕而不問。

translations.literal: Zhen pardoned and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen pardoned him and pursued the matter no further.

sentences.zh: 後徵為都牧尚書。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as Director of Pasturage in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Director of Pasturage in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈侍中、儀同三司，諡簡公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Attendant-in-ordinary and given the same ceremonial rank as the Three Dukes; posthumous title Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Attendant-in-ordinary with the ceremonial rank of the Three Dukes, styled Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 有八子。

translations.literal: He had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Eight sons survived him.

sentences.zh: 第五子瑞。

translations.literal: The fifth son Rui.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth son was Rui.

sentences.zh: 初瑞母尹氏，有娠致傷。

translations.literal: At first Rui's mother the Lady Yin, while pregnant, suffered an injury.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's mother Lady Yin had been injured while carrying him.

sentences.zh: 後畫寢，夢一老翁具衣冠告之曰：「吾賜汝一子，汝勿憂之。

translations.literal: Later while painting in her chamber she dreamed an old man in full cap and robes told her: "I grant you a son; do not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Later, resting in her chamber, she dreamed an old man in court dress who said, "I give you a son—do not grieve."

sentences.zh: 」寤而私喜。

translations.literal: When she awoke she rejoiced in private.
translations.idiomatic: She woke and rejoiced in secret.

sentences.zh: 又問筮者，筮者曰：「大吉。

translations.literal: She again asked a diviner; the diviner said: "Great fortune."
translations.idiomatic: She consulted a diviner, who said, "Great fortune."

sentences.zh: 」未幾而生瑞，禎以為協夢，故名瑞，字天賜。

translations.literal: Before long Rui was born; Zhen thought it accorded with the dream, and therefore named him Rui, style Tiansi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Rui was born; Zhen took it as fulfillment of the dream and named him Rui, style Tiansi.

sentences.zh: 位太中大夫。

translations.literal: He held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常卿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 儀弟烈，剛武有智略。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Lie was fierce in martial bearing and had wisdom and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's brother Lie was bold in war and shrewd in counsel.

sentences.zh: 元紹之逆，百僚莫敢有聲，惟烈行出外，詐附紹募執太宗。

translations.literal: In Yuan Shao's rebellion the hundred officials did not dare speak; only Lie went out, feigned attachment to Shao, and enlisted men to seize Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuan Shao's revolt the court was mute; only Lie went abroad, pretended to join Shao, and raised men to seize Emperor Taizong.

sentences.zh: 紹信之，自延秋門出，遂迎立太宗。

translations.literal: Shao trusted him; he himself went out from Yanchiu Gate and then welcomed and established Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shao trusted him; Lie led his men out through Yanchiu Gate and brought Emperor Taizong to the throne.

sentences.zh: 以功進爵陰平王。

translations.literal: For merit his title was advanced to Prince of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was raised to Prince of Yinping.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰熹。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Xi.

sentences.zh: 子裘襲。

translations.literal: His son Qiu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiu inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 烈弟觚，勇略有膽氣，少與兄儀從太祖，侍衞左右。

translations.literal: Lie's younger brother Gu was brave in stratagem and had daring spirit; in youth he followed his elder brother Yi in attending Taizu and guarded left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's brother Gu was bold and resourceful; in youth he followed Yi in serving Taizu as a guardsman.

sentences.zh: 使於慕容垂，垂末年，政在羣下，遂止觚以求賂。

translations.literal: He was sent to Murong Chui; in Chui's last years government lay with subordinates, and they therefore detained Gu to demand a bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Murong Chui, he found the court in Chui's last years controlled by underlings who detained him and demanded a bribe.

sentences.zh: 太祖絕之。

translations.literal: Taizu broke off relations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu broke off relations with Yan.

sentences.zh: 觚率左右數十騎，殺其衞將走歸。

translations.literal: Gu led several tens of horsemen on his left and right, killed their guard general, and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Gu rode out with a few dozen men, killed the guard commander, and fled home.

sentences.zh: 為慕容寶所執，歸中山，垂待之逾厚。

translations.literal: He was seized by Murong Bao, returned to Zhongshan, and Chui treated him with ever greater generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao captured him and brought him back to Zhongshan, where Chui treated him with growing favor.

sentences.zh: 觚因留心學業，誦讀經書數十萬言，垂之國人咸稱重之。

translations.literal: Gu thereupon devoted himself to study, recited and read several hundred thousand words of the classics, and Chui's countrymen all praised and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu applied himself to learning, mastered hundreds of thousands of words of the classics, and won esteem throughout Yan.

sentences.zh: 太祖之討中山，慕容普驎既自立，遂害觚以固眾心，太祖聞之哀慟。

translations.literal: When Taizu attacked Zhongshan, Murong Pulong had already set himself up and then killed Gu to firm the hearts of the multitude; when Taizu heard of it he grieved bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched on Zhongshan, Murong Pulong, having seized power, killed Gu to bind his followers to him; Taizu mourned deeply when he heard.

sentences.zh: 及平中山，發普驎柩，斬其尸，收議害觚者高霸、程同等，皆夷五族，以大刃剉殺之。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he opened Pulong's coffin, cut down his corpse, seized Gao Ba, Cheng Tong, and others who had plotted Gu's death, and exterminated all five degrees of kin; he had them killed by hacking with great blades.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he opened Pulong's coffin and hacked the corpse apart, seized Gao Ba, Cheng Tong, and the rest who had plotted Gu's death, exterminated their clans to the fifth degree, and had them cut apart with great blades.

sentences.zh: 乃改葬觚，追諡秦愍王，封子夔為豫章王以紹觚。

translations.literal: He then reburied Gu, posthumously enfeoffed him Prince of Qin Min, and enfeoffed his son Kui Prince of Yuzhang to continue Gu's line.
translations.idiomatic: He reburied Gu as Prince of Qin Min and enfeoffed his son Kui as Prince of Yuzhang to continue the line.

sentences.zh: 常山王遵，昭成子壽鳩之子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Changshan Zun was the son of Zhaocheng's son Shoujiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zun, Prince of Changshan, descended from Zhaocheng through his son Shoujiu.

sentences.zh: 少而壯勇，不拘小節。

translations.literal: From youth he was strong and brave and did not bind himself to small proprieties.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was fierce and free of petty scruple.

sentences.zh: 太祖初，有佐命勳，賜爵略陽公。

translations.literal: In early Taizu he had merit in assisting the founding mandate and was granted the title Duke of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizu's early days he helped establish the realm and was made Duke of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶之敗也，別率騎七百邀其歸路，由是有參合之捷。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao was defeated he separately led seven hundred horsemen to intercept his line of retreat; thereby there was the victory at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao was routed he took seven hundred horsemen to block the retreat and won the victory at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 及平中山，拜尚書左僕射，加侍中，領勃海之合口。

translations.literal: When Zhongshan was pacified he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, added Attendant-in-ordinary, and given charge of Hekou in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongshan fell he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Attendant-in-ordinary, and held Hekou in Bohai.

sentences.zh: [5]及博陵、勃海羣盜起，遵討平之。

translations.literal: [5] When bandits rose in Boling and Bohai, Zun attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: [5] When bandits rose in Boling and Bohai he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 遷州牧，封常山王。

translations.literal: He was moved to Inspector and enfeoffed Prince of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Inspector and enfeoffed Prince of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 遵好酒，天賜四年，坐醉亂失禮於太原公主，賜死，葬以庶人禮。

translations.literal: Zun loved wine; in the fourth year of Tiansi, for drunken disorder and breach of propriety toward the Princess of Taiyuan, he was granted death and buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zun drank heavily; in the fourth year of Tiansi he insulted the Princess of Taiyuan while drunk, was granted death, and was buried with common rites.

sentences.zh: 子素，太宗從母所生，特見親寵。

translations.literal: His son Su was born of Emperor Taizong's mother's younger sister and was especially favored.
translations.idiomatic: His son Su was born to Emperor Taizong's maternal aunt and was singularly favored.

sentences.zh: 少引內侍，頻歷顯官，賜爵尚安公，拜外都大官。

translations.literal: From youth he was brought within to attend; he repeatedly held eminent office, was granted the title Duke of Shang'an, and was appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Court.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from youth in the inner palace, he rose through high office, was made Duke of Shang'an, and became Grand Officer of the Outer Court.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，復襲爵。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu he again inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizu's accession he inherited the title anew.

sentences.zh: 休屠郁原等叛，素討之，斬渠率，徙千餘家於涿鹿之陽，立平原郡以處之。

translations.literal: When the Xiutu of Yuyuan and others rebelled, Su attacked them, beheaded the chieftain, and moved more than a thousand households to the south of Zhuolu, establishing Pingyuan commandery to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xiutu of Yuyuan rebelled he crushed them, beheaded their leader, and resettled more than a thousand households south of Zhuolu in the new Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 及平統萬，以素有威懷之略，拜假節、征西大將軍以鎮之。

translations.literal: When Tongwan was pacified, because Su had authority to win hearts by awe, he was appointed with staff of authority as Grand General Who Pacifies the West to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: After Tongwan fell his reputation for stern mercy won him appointment as Grand General Who Pacifies the West with full authority to hold the region.

sentences.zh: 後拜內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Officer of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Grand Officer of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，務崇寬征，罷諸雜調。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne he devoted himself to lenient rule and abolished miscellaneous levies.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Gaozong's accession he pursued a policy of leniency and abolished miscellaneous levies.

sentences.zh: 有司奏國用不足，固請復之，惟素曰：「臣聞『百姓不足，君孰與足。

translations.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that state revenue was insufficient and firmly requested their restoration; only Su said: "Your servant has heard, 'When the people are insufficient, with whom shall the ruler be sufficient?'"
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported the treasury empty and begged to restore the levies; only Su said, "I have heard that when the people lack, the ruler cannot abound."

sentences.zh: 』」帝善而從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and held to Su's counsel.

sentences.zh: 詔羣臣議定皇子名，素及司徒陸麗議曰：「古帝王之制名，其體有五：有信，有義，有象，有假，有類。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to discuss fixing the princes' names; Su and Minister of State Lu Li deliberated, saying: "In ancient emperors' and kings' institution of names, the form has five kinds: there is trust, there is righteousness, there is image, there is borrowing, and there is category.
translations.idiomatic: The court was ordered to name the newborn princes; Su and Minister of State Lu Li argued that ancient rulers used five kinds of names: trust, righteousness, image, borrowing, and category.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下當盛明之運，應昌發之期，誕生皇子，宜以德命。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that Your Majesty stands in a flourishing bright fortune, answers a season of glorious expansion, and has begotten a prince; he should be named by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They urged that at this flourishing season, when Your Majesty had begotten a prince, the child should receive a name drawn from virtue.

sentences.zh: 」高宗從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong agreed.

sentences.zh: 素宗屬之懿，又年老，帝每引入，訪以治國政事。

translations.literal: Su was eminent among the clan kindred and was also old; the emperor each time brought him in and consulted him on governing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Su stood foremost among the clan and was by then aged; the emperor often summoned him to counsel on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 固辭疾歸第。

translations.literal: He firmly declined on grounds of illness and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and withdrew to his home.

sentences.zh: 雅性方正，居官五十載，終始如一，時論賢之。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and square; in office for fifty years he was the same from first to last; opinion of the time praised him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Upright by nature, he served fifty years without change, and his age called him worthy.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰康，陪葬金陵，配饗廟庭。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Kang; he was buried with honor at Jinling and received sacrifice in the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was styled Kang, buried at Jinling, and honored with temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 長子可悉陵，年十七，從世祖獵，遇一猛虎，陵遂空手搏之以獻。

translations.literal: His eldest son Kesiling, aged seventeen, followed Shizu on the hunt, met a fierce tiger, and Kesiling then fought it empty-handed and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Kesiling, seventeen, joined Shizu on a hunt, met a tiger, and brought it down bare-handed as tribute.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「汝才力絕人，當為國立事，勿如此也。

translations.literal: Shizu said: "Your talent and strength are unmatched; you should establish deeds for the state—do not act thus."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Your strength is matchless—serve the state with deeds, not with stunts like this."

sentences.zh: 」即拜內行阿干。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Inner Aghan.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once made Inner Aghan.

sentences.zh: 又從平涼州。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the pacification of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 沮渠茂虔令一驍將與陵相擊，兩槊皆折。

translations.literal: Juqu Maoqian ordered a fierce general to engage Kesiling; both spears broke.
translations.idiomatic: Juqu Maoqian sent a champion against Kesiling; both spears shattered.

sentences.zh: 陵抽箭射之，墜馬，陵恐其救至，未及拔劍，以刀子戾其頸，使身首異處。

translations.literal: Kesiling drew an arrow and shot him; he fell from his horse; Kesiling feared rescue would arrive, and before he could draw his sword he used a knife to cut across the neck and made body and head separate places.
translations.idiomatic: Kesiling shot him from the saddle; before reinforcements could arrive and before he could draw his sword he slit the man's throat with a knife and severed head from body.

sentences.zh: 世祖壯之，即日拜都幢將，封暨陽子。

translations.literal: Shizu admired him; that same day he was appointed Chief of the Imperial Banners and enfeoffed Marquis of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu admired the feat and that same day made him Chief of the Imperial Banners and Marquis of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 卒于中軍都將。

translations.literal: He died while Chief General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as Chief General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 弟陪斤，襲爵，坐事國除。

translations.literal: His younger brother Peijin succeeded to the title; for an offense the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Peijin inherited the title but lost the fief for a crime.

sentences.zh: 陪斤子昭，小字阿倪，尚書張彝引兼殿中郎。

translations.literal: Peijin's son Zhao, childhood name Ani, was brought in by Zhang Yi of the Masters of Writing as concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Peijin's son Zhao, called Ani in youth, was introduced by Master of Writing Zhang Yi as a concurrent palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 高祖將為齊郡王簡舉哀，[6]而昭乃作宮懸。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was about to observe mourning for Prince of Qi Jun, Zhao instead composed palace music.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was to mourn Prince of Qi Jun, Zhao composed palace music instead.

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒，詔曰：「阿倪愚騃，誰引為郎！

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly angered and ordered: "Ani is stupid and dull—who introduced him as attendant!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu raged and said, "Ani is a fool—who made him an attendant!"

sentences.zh: 」於是黜彝白衣守尚書，昭遂停廢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhang Yi was demoted to commoner to guard the Masters of Writing, and Zhao was then stopped and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi was reduced to commoner rank to serve in the Masters of Writing, and Zhao was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，昭從弟暉親寵用事，稍遷左丞。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizong's time Zhao's cousin Hui was close in favor and held power; he was gradually promoted to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizong his cousin Hui held favor and power, and Zhao rose by degrees to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 世宗崩，于忠執政，昭為黃門郎，又曲事之。

translations.literal: When Shizong died Yu Zhong held government; Zhao was Yellow Gate Attendant and again curried favor with him.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's death Yu Zhong seized power; Zhao served as Yellow Gate Attendant and fawned on him again.

sentences.zh: 忠專權擅威，枉陷忠賢，多昭所指導也。

translations.literal: Zhong monopolized authority and abused power, wrongfully entrapped loyal worthies—many were at Zhao's guidance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong ruled by force and ruined loyal men, often on Zhao's prompting.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，為尚書、河南尹。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was Director of the Masters of Writing and Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Ling he became Director of the Masters of Writing and Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 聾而佷戾，理務峭急，所在患之。

translations.literal: Deaf and obstinate, in handling affairs he was harsh and urgent; wherever he went he was a plague.
translations.idiomatic: Deaf and brutal, he ran affairs with savage haste and was dreaded wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 尋出為雍州刺史，在州貪虐，大為人害。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Inspector of Yongzhou; in the province he was greedy and cruel and greatly harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Inspector of Yongzhou, where his greed and cruelty did great harm.

sentences.zh: 後入為尚書，諂事劉騰，進號征西將軍。

translations.literal: Later he entered court as Director of the Masters of Writing, fawned on Liu Teng, and was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the Masters of Writing, he flattered Liu Teng and was raised to General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 納貨元叉，所以贈禮優越。

translations.literal: He paid bribes to Yuan Cha, and therefore the posthumous gifts were exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: He had bribed Yuan Cha, and so his funeral honors were lavish.

sentences.zh: 昭弟紹，字醜倫。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Shao, style Choulun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's brother Shao, style Choulun.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 紹斷決不避強禦。

translations.literal: Shao in judgment did not avoid the strong and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: In judgment Shao never shrank from the powerful.

sentences.zh: 世宗詔令檢趙脩獄，以脩佞幸，因此遂加杖罰，令其致死。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered him to examine Zhao Xiu's prison case; because Xiu was a favorite flatterer, he therefore added cudgel punishment and ordered him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered him to review Zhao Xiu's case; Xiu was a court favorite, so Shao added beatings and drove the sentence to death.

sentences.zh: 帝責紹不重聞。

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Shao for not reporting again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Shao for not seeking a second report.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「脩姦佞甚於董賢，臣若不因釁除之，恐陛下復被哀帝之名。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Xiu's treachery and flattery exceeded Dong Xian's; if your servant did not seize the occasion to remove him, I fear Your Majesty would again bear the name of Emperor Ai."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Xiu's villainy outdid Dong Xian's; had I not seized the chance to remove him, Your Majesty might have gone the way of Emperor Ai."

sentences.zh: 」以其言正，遂不罪焉。

translations.literal: Because his words were upright, he was therefore not punished.
translations.idiomatic: His words were just, and the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 及出，廣平王懷拜紹，賀曰：「阿翁乃皇家之正直，雖朱雲、汲黯何以仰過。

translations.literal: When he went out, Prince of Guangping Huai bowed to Shao and congratulated him, saying: "Uncle is the integrity of the imperial house—how could Zhu Yun and Ji An even be looked up to in comparison!"
translations.idiomatic: As he left, Prince of Guangping Huai bowed to him and said, "Uncle, you are the house's conscience—Zhu Yun and Ji An are not fit to be named beside you!"

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「但恨戮之稍晚，以為愧耳。

translations.literal: Shao said: "I only regret that the killing was somewhat late; that is my shame."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "I only regret the killing came late—that is my shame."

sentences.zh: 」卒於涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 陪斤弟忠，字仙德。

translations.literal: Peijin's younger brother Zhong, style Xiande.
translations.idiomatic: Peijin's brother Zhong, style Xiande.

sentences.zh: 少沉厚，以忠謹聞。

translations.literal: From youth he was deep and steady; he was known for loyalty and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was grave and steady, famed for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 高祖時，累遷右僕射，賜爵城陽公，加侍中、鎮西將軍，有翼贊之勤，百僚咸敬之。

translations.literal: In Gaozu's time he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director, granted the title Duke of Chengyang, added Attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Guards the West; he had merit in assisting and supporting, and the hundred officials all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he rose to Right Vice Director, was made Duke of Chengyang, Attendant-in-ordinary, and General Who Guards the West, and won the respect of the whole court for steadfast service.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，病篤辭退，養疾於高柳。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe his illness was grave and he declined office; he nursed his illness at Gaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe, gravely ill, he resigned and went to nurse his health at Gaoliu.

sentences.zh: 輿駕親送都門之外，賜雜綵二百匹，羣僚侍臣執別者，莫不涕泣。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage personally escorted him beyond the capital gate and granted two hundred bolts of mixed silks; the attending ministers who took leave of him all wept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor escorted him beyond the capital gate in person, gave him two hundred bolts of silk, and the ministers who bade him farewell wept.

sentences.zh: 及卒，皆悼惜之。

translations.literal: When he died all mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court mourned him.

sentences.zh: 諡曰宣，命有司為立碑銘。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Xuan; he was ordered to have the responsible officials erect a stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: He was styled Xuan, and the throne ordered officials to raise a memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 有十七子。

translations.literal: He had seventeen sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left seventeen sons.

sentences.zh: 子盛，字始興，襲爵，位謁者僕射。

translations.literal: His son Sheng, styled Shixing, inherited the title and served as Supervisor of Palace Ushers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng, styled Shixing, inherited the fief and rose to Supervisor of Palace Ushers.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 盛弟壽興，[8]少聰慧好學。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing, [8] was clever and fond of learning from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing, [8] was bright and bookish from boyhood.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，為徐州刺史，在官貪虐，失於人心。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Shizong's reign he was made Regional Inspector of Xuzhou; in office he was greedy and cruel and lost the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Shizong's reign he became inspector of Xuzhou; greedy and brutal in office, he lost the people.

sentences.zh: 其從兄侍中暉，深害其能，因譖之於帝，詔尚書崔亮馳驛檢覆。

translations.literal: His cousin, Palace Attendant Hui, deeply resented his ability and slandered him to the emperor; an edict ordered Master of Writing Cui Liang to ride post-horses and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Palace Attendant Hui, who envied his talent, denounced him to the throne; Cui Liang of the Masters of Writing was ordered to investigate by express relay.

sentences.zh: 亮發日，受暉旨，遂鞭撻三寡婦，令其自誣，稱壽興壓己為婢。

translations.literal: The day Liang set out he took Hui's instructions and had three widows flogged until they falsely accused themselves, saying Shouxing had forced them to be his bondmaids.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he departed Liang followed Hui's orders, had three widows beaten until they confessed that Shouxing had pressed them into servitude.

sentences.zh: 壽興終恐不免，乃令其外弟中兵參軍薛脩義將車十乘，運小麥經其禁之旁。

translations.literal: Shouxing, fearing he could not escape, had his wife's younger brother, Army Staff Officer Xue Xiuyi, bring ten carts hauling wheat past his place of detention.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced he would not escape, Shouxing had his brother-in-law Xue Xiuyi, a staff officer, drive ten carts of wheat past the compound where he was held.

sentences.zh: 壽興因踰牆出。

translations.literal: Shouxing climbed over the wall and got out.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing scaled the wall and fled.

sentences.zh: 脩義以大木函盛壽興，其上加麥，載之而出。

translations.literal: Xiuyi put Shouxing in a great wooden chest, heaped wheat on top, and hauled him away.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuyi hid him in a great wooden chest, piled wheat on top, and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 遂至河東，匿脩義家。

translations.literal: He reached Hedong and hid in Xiuyi's house.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Hedong and lay hidden in Xiuyi's home.

sentences.zh: 逢赦，乃出見世宗，自陳為暉所譖，世宗亦更無所責。

translations.literal: When an amnesty was proclaimed he came out to see Emperor Shizong, confessed that Hui had slandered him, and the emperor imposed no further penalty.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he appeared before Shizong, said Hui had framed him, and was not punished further.

sentences.zh: 初，壽興為中庶子時，王顯在東官，賤，因公事壽興杖之三十。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouxing was Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, Wang Xian was in the Eastern Palace in a low station; on official business Shouxing had him beaten thirty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while Shouxing served as junior mentor in the Eastern Palace, Wang Xian held a low post; on official grounds Shouxing had him thrashed thirty strokes.

sentences.zh: 及顯有寵，為御史中尉，奏壽興在家每有怨言，誹謗朝廷。

translations.literal: When Xian won favor and became Censor-in-Chief, he memorialized that Shouxing at home often murmured complaints and slandered the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian grew powerful as Censor-in-Chief, he reported that Shouxing grumbled at home and reviled the court.

sentences.zh: 因帝極飲無所覺悟，遂奏其事，命帝注可，直付壽興賜死。

translations.literal: Because the emperor was deep in drink and unaware, he submitted the matter, had the emperor write "approved," and sent it straight to Shouxing ordering him to die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was drunk and unheeding; Xian submitted the charge, had him scrawl approval, and sent the order straight to Shouxing to die.

sentences.zh: 帝書半不成字，當時見者亦知非本心，但懼暉等威，不敢申拔。

translations.literal: The emperor's hand formed only half the characters; those present knew it was not his true will, but they feared Hui's power and dared not speak up.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's characters were half-formed; witnesses knew his heart was not in it, yet they feared Hui and dared not intervene.

sentences.zh: 及行刑日，顯自往看之。

translations.literal: On the day of execution Xian went in person to watch.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of execution Xian went to watch in person.

sentences.zh: 壽興命筆自作墓誌銘曰：「洛陽男子，姓元名景，有道無時，其年不永。

translations.literal: Shouxing ordered brush and wrote his own epitaph: "A man of Luoyang, surname Yuan, given name Jing—virtue without its season, his years not long."
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing called for brush and ink and wrote his own epitaph: "A man of Luoyang, surname Yuan, given name Jing—virtue without its hour, years cut short."

sentences.zh: 」餘文多不載。

translations.literal: " The rest of the text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " The remainder is not fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 顧謂其子曰：「我棺中可著百張紙，筆兩枚，吾欲訟顯於地下。

translations.literal: He turned to his son and said, "Put a hundred sheets of paper and two brushes in my coffin—I mean to sue Xian in the underworld.
translations.idiomatic: He told his son, "Lay a hundred sheets of paper and two brushes in my coffin. I intend to bring suit against Xian below."

sentences.zh: 若高祖之靈有知，百日內必取顯，如遂無知，亦何足戀。

translations.literal: If Gaozu's spirit has knowledge, within a hundred days he will surely take Xian; if there is truly no knowledge, what is there to cling to?"
translations.idiomatic: If Gaozu's spirit sees, he will take Xian within a hundred days; if the dead know nothing, why linger at all?"

sentences.zh: 」及世宗崩，顯尋被殺。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Shizong died, Xian was soon killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong died, Xian was killed soon after.

sentences.zh: 壽興之死，時論亦以為前任中尉彈高

translations.literal: As for Shouxing's death, opinion of the time also held that the former Censor-in-Chief's impeachment of Gao
translations.idiomatic: When Shouxing died, contemporaries also blamed the former censor's impeachment of Gao

translations.literal: 〈lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈lacuna〉

sentences.zh: 讒諷所致。

translations.literal: was what led to slander and brought the affair about.
translations.idiomatic: for the slander that had set the tragedy in motion.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，三公郎中崔鴻上疏理壽興，詔追雪，贈豫州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court, Gentleman of the Three Excellencies Cui Hong memorialized to clear Shouxing; an edict posthumously exonerated him, made him posthumous Regional Inspector of Yuzhou, and gave the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling ruled, Cui Hong of the Three Excellencies petitioned to clear him; the court posthumously exonerated him, made him inspector of Yuzhou, and styled him Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 壽興弟益生，少亡。

translations.literal: Shouxing's younger brother Yisheng died young.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yisheng died in youth.

sentences.zh: 忠弟德，封河間公。

translations.literal: Zhong's younger brother De was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's brother De was made Duke of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮南將軍，贈曹州刺史。

translations.literal: He died while General Who Guards the South and was posthumously made Regional Inspector of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as General Who Guards the South and was posthumously made inspector of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 德子悝，潁川太守。

translations.literal: De's son Ti was Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: De's son Ti served as administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 卒於光州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He died as Regional Inspector of Guang Province; posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He died as inspector of Guang and was posthumously styled Gong.

sentences.zh: 忠子暉，[11]字景襲。

translations.literal: Zhong's son Hui, [11] styled Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's son Hui, [11] styled Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 少沉敏，頗涉文史。

translations.literal: From youth he was grave and keen and had some knowledge of letters and history.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was grave and quick, with some learning in letters and history.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，拜尚書主客郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne he was appointed Master of Writing, Director of Foreign Guests.
translations.idiomatic: At Shizong's accession he became Director of Foreign Guests in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 巡省風俗，還，奏事稱旨，為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: On a tour inspecting local customs he returned, reported to the throne to satisfaction, and was made Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After touring local customs he reported to the throne to satisfaction and was made attendant gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖遷洛，而在位舊貴皆難於移徙，時欲和合眾情，遂許冬則居南，夏便居北。

translations.literal: At first, when Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, the old nobles in office all found relocation hard; to reconcile feelings the court then allowed winter residence in the south and summer in the north.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu moved the capital to Luoyang, old nobles balked at relocation; to soothe them the court allowed winters in the south and summers in the north.

sentences.zh: 世宗頗惑左右之言，外人遂有還北之問，至乃牓賣田宅，不安其居。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong was much swayed by attendants' words; outsiders then raised talk of returning north, even posting notices to sell fields and houses, unsettled in their dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong heeded his attendants; rumor spread of a return north, notices went up to sell houses, and people could not settle.

sentences.zh: 暉乃請間言事。

translations.literal: Hui then requested a private audience to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked for a private audience.

sentences.zh: 世宗曰：「先皇遷都之日，本期冬南夏北，朕欲聿遵成詔，故有外人之論。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said, "When the late emperor moved the capital he planned winter south and summer north; I wish to follow that settled edict—hence outsiders' talk."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong said, "When the late emperor moved the capital he meant winter south and summer north. I mean to keep that edict—hence the talk outside."

sentences.zh: 」暉曰：「先皇移都，為百姓戀土，故發冬夏二居之詔，權寧物意耳。

translations.literal: Hui said, "The late emperor moved the capital because the people clung to their native soil; he issued the winter-summer dual residence edict only to ease their minds for the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Hui answered, "The move was for people who clung to their soil; the dual-residence edict was only to calm them for a time.

sentences.zh: 乃是當時之言，實非先皇深意。

translations.literal: That was language for the moment, not the late emperor's true intent.
translations.idiomatic: That was speech for the hour, not his true intent.

sentences.zh: 且北來遷人，安居歲久，公私計立，無復還情。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who came north have dwelt in peace many years; public and private plans are set—there is no thought of return.
translations.idiomatic: Those who came north have lived here for years; households and offices are settled—no one wishes to return.

sentences.zh: 陛下終高祖定鼎之業，勿信邪臣不然之說。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should complete Gaozu's work of fixing the tripod—do not trust wicked ministers' contrary talk."
translations.idiomatic: Finish Gaozu's work of fixing the capital. Do not heed wicked ministers who say otherwise."

sentences.zh: 」世宗從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 再遷侍中，領右衞將軍，雖無補益，深被親寵。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Palace Attendant and concurrent General of the Right Guard; though he brought no real benefit, he was deeply favored.
translations.idiomatic: He rose again to palace attendant and general of the right guard; though he did little good, favor ran deep.

sentences.zh: 凡在禁中要密之事，暉別奉旨藏之於櫃，唯暉入乃開，其餘侍中、黃門莫有知者。

translations.literal: Whatever secret matters arose within the forbidden precinct, Hui alone received orders and stored them in a cabinet—only when Hui entered was it opened; none of the other attendants or yellow-gate officers knew.
translations.idiomatic: Secret business of the inner palace went into a cabinet on Hui's orders alone; only he could open it—other attendants and yellow-gate officers knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 侍中盧昶亦蒙恩眄，故時人號曰「餓虎將軍，飢鷹侍中」。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Lu Chang also received favoring glances, so people of the time called them "the starving-tiger general and the hungry-eagle attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Lu Chang shared the favor, and people nicknamed them "the starving-tiger general and the hungry-eagle attendant."

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，納貨用官，皆有定價，大郡二千匹，次郡一千匹，下郡五百匹，其餘受職各有差，天下號曰「市曹」。

translations.literal: He was moved to Minister of the Imperial Secretariat; selling offices for bribes had fixed prices—great commanderies two thousand bolts, middling one thousand, lesser five hundred; other posts had their own scales; the realm called it the "market bureau."
translations.idiomatic: As minister of the imperial secretariat he sold offices at fixed rates—two thousand bolts for a great commandery, one thousand for a middling, five hundred for a lesser—and the realm called his ministry the market bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，下州之日，連車載物，發信都，至湯陰間，首尾相繼，道路不斷。

translations.literal: Sent out as Regional Inspector of Jizhou, the day he left his post a train of carts loaded goods from Xindu to Tangyin without break along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Made inspector of Jizhou, he left office with carts in an unbroken line from Xindu to Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 其車少脂角，即於道上所逢之牛，生截取角以充其用。

translations.literal: When a cart lacked grease or horn, he cut horns live from any ox met on the road to supply the need.
translations.idiomatic: When carts lacked grease or horn fittings, his men cut horns from oxen met on the road.

sentences.zh: 暉檢括丁戶，聽其歸首，出調絹五萬匹。

translations.literal: Hui audited registered households, allowed self-report of heads, and levied fifty thousand bolts of silk in tax.
translations.idiomatic: He audited household registers, allowed self-report of dependents, and levied fifty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 然聚斂無極，百姓患之。

translations.literal: Yet his exactions knew no limit and the people suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his levies never ceased, and the people groaned under them.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，徵拜尚書左僕射，詔攝吏部選事。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Suzong's reign he was summoned as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and ordered to handle Secretariat selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Suzong's accession he was recalled as left vice director of the Masters of Writing and told to handle personnel selection.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣聞治人之本，實委牧守之官。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "I have heard that the root of governing men lies in entrusting prefects and governors.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted: "The root of rule lies in prefects and governors.

sentences.zh: 得其才則政平物理，失其人則訟興怨結。

translations.literal: With the right talent, government is level and things are ordered; with the wrong men, lawsuits rise and resentment knots.
translations.idiomatic: Find the right men and government runs level; choose wrongly and suits multiply and resentment knots.

sentences.zh: 自非察訪善惡，明加貶賞，將何以黜彼貪怠，陟此清勤也。

translations.literal: Unless one inspects good and evil and clearly rewards or punishes, how will one dismiss the greedy and idle and advance the pure and diligent?
translations.idiomatic: Without inspection and clear reward and punishment, how dismiss the greedy and raise the diligent?

sentences.zh: 竊以大使巡省，必廣迎送之費；

translations.literal: I venture that grand envoys on inspection tours must broaden costs of welcome and send-off;
translations.idiomatic: Grand inspection envoys widen welcome and send-off costs;

sentences.zh: 御史馳糾，頗回威濫之刑。

translations.literal: censors who ride post to impeach often bend authority into abusive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: censors who ride post to impeach often bend authority into abusive punishment.

sentences.zh: 且暫爾往還，理不委悉，縱有簡舉，良未平當。

translations.literal: Moreover, brief comings and goings cannot grasp matters fully; even when there are selections and recommendations, they are often not fair.
translations.idiomatic: Brief tours cannot grasp affairs fully; even when names are raised, justice is uneven.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜令三司、八座、侍中、黃門，各布耳目，外訪州鎮牧將治人，守令能不。

translations.literal: I think the Three Excellencies, the Eight Seats, attendants, and yellow-gate officers should each set out eyes and ears, inquire abroad into how provincial and garrison governors, military commanders, and magistrates govern men, and whether prefects and county chiefs are capable.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Three Excellencies, Eight Seats, attendants, and yellow-gate officers each set eyes and ears abroad to learn how governors, commanders, and magistrates rule.

sentences.zh: 若德教有方，清白獨著，宜以名聞，即加褒陟。

translations.literal: If moral teaching is well ordered and purity stands alone, they should be named and promptly promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Where teaching is sound and conduct pure, name them and promote them at once.

sentences.zh: 若治績無効，貪暴遠聞，亦便示牒，登加貶退。

translations.literal: If governing achievement is void and greed or cruelty is heard from afar, show the document and register demotion or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Where rule fails or greed and cruelty travel far, publish the order and demote or dismiss.

sentences.zh: 如此則不出庭戶，坐知四方，端委垂拱，明賞審罰矣。

translations.literal: Thus without leaving the court hall one would sit knowing the four quarters—dignified, hands folded, with clear reward and careful punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Then without leaving the hall you would know the realm—seated in dignity, with reward clear and punishment measured."

sentences.zh: 」又表以「御史之職，鷹鸇是任，必逞爪牙，有所噬搏。

translations.literal: He also submitted that "the censor's office is fit for hawks and falcons—they must bare claw and fang and seize something to tear.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that censors are hawks and falcons—they must bare claw and seize prey.

sentences.zh: 若選後生年少、血氣方剛者，恐其輕肆勁直，傷物處廣。

translations.literal: If one chooses young men fresh in blood and vigor, I fear their rash forthrightness will wound widely.
translations.idiomatic: Choose hot-blooded youths and they will wound too widely.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜簡宿官經事、忠良平慎者為之。

translations.literal: I think one should choose veteran officials experienced in affairs, loyal, steady, and even-tempered."
translations.idiomatic: Choose seasoned officials who are loyal, steady, and even-tempered."

sentences.zh: 」詔付外，依此施行。

translations.literal: " An edict sent this outside and ordered implementation accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent the plan out for implementation.

sentences.zh: 後詔暉與任城王澄、京兆王愉、東平王匡共決門下大事。

translations.literal: Later an edict had Hui, with Prince of Rencheng Cheng, Prince of Jingzhao Yu, and Prince of Dongping Kuang, jointly decide great affairs of the Gate Department.
translations.idiomatic: Later Hui was ordered, with Prince Cheng of Rencheng, Prince Yu of Jingzhao, and Prince Kuang of Dongping, to decide great Gate Department affairs together.

sentences.zh: 暉又上書論政要：「其一曰：御史之職，務使得賢，必得其人，不拘階秩，久於其事，責其成功。

translations.literal: Hui again submitted a letter on governing essentials: "First: the censor's office must obtain worthy men—must get the right person, not bound by rank and grade, long in the post, held to success.
translations.idiomatic: Hui wrote again on essentials of rule: "First, censors must obtain worthy men—the right person, not bound by rank, long in post, held to results.

sentences.zh: 其二曰：安人寧邊，觀時而動，頃來邊將，亡遠大之略，貪萬一之功，楚梁之好未聞，而蠶婦之怨屢結，斯乃庸人所為，銳於姦利之所致也。

translations.literal: Second: settle the people and quiet the borders, act as times require. Lately frontier generals have lost far-reaching strategy and grasp at one-in-ten-thousand gains; the good will of Chu and Liang is unheard of, while silkworm-wives' grievances knot again and again—this is what mediocrities do, keen for illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Second, settle people and quiet borders and move as times require. Frontier generals lately grasp at trifling gains; goodwill with Chu and Liang is unheard of while silkworm-wives' grievances knot again—mediocrities keen for illicit profit.

sentences.zh: 平吳之計，自有良圖，不在於一城一戍也。

translations.literal: The plan to pacify Wu has its own good design—not in one city or one garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to pacify Wu has its own design—not in one city or one garrison.

sentences.zh: 又河北數州，國之基本，飢荒多年，戶口流散。

translations.literal: Moreover, several Hebei provinces are the state's foundation; famine has run many years and households have scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Several Hebei provinces are the state's foundation; famine has run for years and households have scattered.

sentences.zh: 方今境上兵復徵發，即如此日，何易舉動。

translations.literal: Now troops on the borders are levied again—even on a day like this, how easy is any move?
translations.idiomatic: Troops on the borders are levied again—even today, how easy is any move?

sentences.zh: 愚謂數年以來，唯宜靜邊以息占役，安人勸農，惠此中夏。

translations.literal: I think that for several years one should only quiet the borders to cease corvée and garrison duty, settle the people and encourage farming, and show grace to this central realm.
translations.idiomatic: For years the sole policy should be quiet borders, end corvée and garrison duty, settle people, encourage farming, and show grace to the central realm.

sentences.zh: 請嚴勅邊將，自今有賊戍求內附者，不聽輒遣援接，皆須表聞，違者雖有功，請以違詔書論。

translations.literal: I ask a stern order to frontier generals: from now on, when bandit garrisons seek to submit inward, do not rashly send relief or receive them—all must be reported; violators, though they have merit, should be judged by violation of edict.
translations.idiomatic: Order frontier generals: when enemy garrisons seek to submit, do not receive them without memorial—violators judged by edict even if they have merit.

sentences.zh: 三曰：國之資儲，唯藉河北。

translations.literal: Third: the state's stores rely only on Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the state's stores rely only on Hebei.

sentences.zh: 飢饉積年，戶口逃散，生長姦詐，因生隱藏，出縮老小，妄注死失。

translations.literal: Famine piled year on year; households fled and scattered; fraud grew and bred concealment—shrinking the old and young in the rolls, falsely registering deaths and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Famine piled up; households fled; fraud bred concealment—shrinking dependents on the rolls and falsely registering deaths.

sentences.zh: 收人租調，割入於己。

translations.literal: Collecting men's land tax and labor levy, they cut portions into their own pockets.
translations.idiomatic: Tax and labor dues were cut into private pockets.

sentences.zh: 人困於下，官損於上。

translations.literal: The people suffer below; the government loses above.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered below; the treasury lost above.

sentences.zh: 自非更立權制，善加檢括，損耗之來，方在未已。
