translations.literal: Unless new flexible rules are set and inspection applied well, the drain will not soon end.
translations.idiomatic: Unless new rules and strict inspection are set, the drain will not end.

sentences.zh: 請求其議，明宣條格。

translations.literal: I ask that this be debated and the articles clearly proclaimed."
translations.idiomatic: Debate this and proclaim the articles clearly."

sentences.zh: 」帝納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 陳留王虔，昭成子紇根之子也。

translations.literal: Chenliu Wang Qian was a son of Heggen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, Prince of Chenliu, was son of Heggen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 少以壯勇知名。

translations.literal: From youth he was known for strength and courage.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was famed for strength and courage.

sentences.zh: 登國初，賜爵陳留公。

translations.literal: At the start of the Dengguo era he was granted the title Duke of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dengguo he was made Duke of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 與衞王儀破黜弗部。

translations.literal: With Prince Wei Yi he broke the Chufu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: With Prince Wei Yi he broke the Chufu tribe.

sentences.zh: 從攻衞辰。

translations.literal: He followed in the attack on Wei Chen.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the attack on Wei Chen.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶來寇，虔絕其左翼。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao came to raid, Qian cut off his left wing.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao raided, Qian cut off his left wing.

sentences.zh: 寶敗，垂恚憤來桑乾。

translations.literal: Bao was defeated; Chui came in rage and resentment to Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was beaten; Chui came to Sanggan in rage.

sentences.zh: 虔勇而輕敵，於陳戰沒。

translations.literal: Qian was brave but slighted the enemy and fell in battle in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Brave but heedless, Qian fell in the field.

sentences.zh: 悅外和內佷。

translations.literal: Yue was outwardly harmonious and inwardly crafty.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was smooth outside and treacherous within.

sentences.zh: 太祖常以桓王死王事，特加親寵。

translations.literal: Taizu, because Prince Huan had died in the king's service, gave him special favor and intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Huan had died in royal service, Taizu favored him with special intimacy.

sentences.zh: 為左將軍，襲封。

translations.literal: He became General of the Left and inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: He became general of the left and inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後為宗師。

translations.literal: Later he was made Imperial Clan Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made imperial clan mentor.

sentences.zh: 悅恃寵驕矜，每謂所親王洛生之徒言曰：「一旦宮車晏駕，吾止避衞公，除此誰在吾前？

translations.literal: Yue relied on favor and was proud; he often told intimates such as Wang Luosheng, "Once the imperial carriage halts forever, I need only yield to the Duke of Wei—who else would stand before me?"
translations.idiomatic: Proud in favor, he told intimates such as Wang Luosheng, "When the throne falls vacant I yield only to the Duke of Wei—who else stands before me?"

sentences.zh: 」衞王儀，美髯，為內外所重，悅故云。

translations.literal: " Prince Wei Yi had a fine beard and was respected within and without—hence Yue's words.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Yi wore a fine beard and was revered within and without—hence the remark.

sentences.zh: 初，姚興之贖狄伯支，悅送之，路由雁門，悅因背誘姦豪，以取其意。

translations.literal: At first, when Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue escorted him; the route passed Yanmen, and Yue secretly won over local strongmen behind their backs to curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue escorted him through Yanmen and secretly won over local strongmen.

sentences.zh: 後遇事譴，逃亡，投雁門，規收豪傑，欲為不軌，為土人執送，太祖恕而不罪。

translations.literal: Later, when he was rebuked for an affair, he fled to Yanmen, plotted to gather heroes and attempt sedition, was seized by locals and sent in; Taizu pardoned and did not punish.
translations.idiomatic: Rebuked later, he fled to Yanmen to gather heroes for sedition; locals seized him and sent him in; Taizu pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，引悅入侍，仍懷姦計，說帝云：「京師雜人，不可保信，宜誅其非類者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he brought Yue in to attend court; Yue still harbored treacherous designs and told the emperor, "The mixed people of the capital cannot be trusted—those not of our kind should be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong brought him to court; Yue still plotted and told him, "The mixed people of the capital cannot be trusted—kill those not of our kind.

sentences.zh: 又雁門人多詐，并可誅之。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of Yanmen are mostly deceitful—they too can all be killed."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yanmen are mostly deceitful—kill them as well."

sentences.zh: 」欲以雪其私忿。

translations.literal: " He wished to settle private grudges.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to settle private scores.

sentences.zh: 太宗不從。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong refused.

sentences.zh: 悅內自疑懼，懷刀入侍，謀為大逆。

translations.literal: Yue inwardly feared and doubted, hid a knife to enter attendance, and plotted great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Fearful within, he entered court with a hidden knife and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 叔孫俊疑之，竊視其懷，有刀，執而賜死。

translations.literal: Shusun Jun suspected him, stole a look at his breast, saw a knife, seized him and ordered him to die.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun Jun suspected him, glimpsed the knife at his breast, seized him, and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 弟崇，世祖詔令襲桓王爵。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chong—Emperor Shizu issued an edict ordering him to inherit Prince Huan's title.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Chong was ordered by Emperor Shizu to inherit Prince Huan's title.

sentences.zh: 崇性沉厚。

translations.literal: Chong's nature was deep and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was grave and steady by nature.

sentences.zh: 初，衞王死後，太祖欲敦宗親之義，詔引諸王子弟入宴。

translations.literal: At first, after Prince Wei's death, Taizu wished to thicken clan kinship and ordered all princes' sons and younger brothers brought in to feast.
translations.idiomatic: After Prince Wei's death Taizu wished to bind the clan and summoned princes' sons to feast.

sentences.zh: 常山王素等三十餘人咸謂與衞王相坐，疑懼，皆出逃遁，將奔蠕蠕，唯崇獨至。

translations.literal: Prince of Changshan Su and more than thirty others all thought they would be implicated with Prince Wei; fearful, they all fled and were about to run to the Rouran—only Chong came alone.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Su of Changshan and more than thirty others feared implication with Prince Wei and fled toward the Rouran—only Chong came.

sentences.zh: 太祖見之甚悅，厚加禮賜，遂寵敬之，素等於是亦安。

translations.literal: Taizu, seeing him, was greatly pleased, richly rewarded him with ritual gifts, and thereafter favored and honored him; Su and the others then were also at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was greatly pleased, honored him richly, and Su and the others took heart.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜并州刺史，有政績。

translations.literal: After long service he was appointed Regional Inspector of Bingzhou and had governing achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In time he became inspector of Bingzhou and governed well.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，別督諸軍出大澤，越涿邪山，威懾漠北。

translations.literal: On campaign against the Rouran he separately directed the armies out through the Great Marsh, crossed Zhuoye Mountain, and awed the northern desert.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against the Rouran he led armies through the Great Marsh, crossed Zhuoye Mountain, and awed the northern desert.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰景王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Prince Jing.

sentences.zh: 子建，襲，降爵為公。

translations.literal: His son Jian inherited; the title was reduced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian inherited; the rank was reduced to duke.

sentences.zh: 位鎮北將軍、懷荒鎮大將。

translations.literal: He held the posts of General Who Guards the North and Great Commander of Huaihuang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as general who guards the north and great commander of Huaihuang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 建子琛，位恒朔二州刺史。

translations.literal: Jian's son Chen was Regional Inspector of Heng and Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Chen was inspector of Heng and Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 琛子翌，尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Chen's son Yi was Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Yi was left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 虔兄顗，性嚴重少言，太祖常敬之。

translations.literal: Qian's elder brother Yi was grave, spoke little, and Taizu often respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's elder brother Yi was grave and sparing of speech; Taizu respected him.

sentences.zh: 雅有謀策，從平中山，以功賜爵蒲城侯、平盧太守，特見寵厚，給鼓吹羽儀，禮同岳牧。

translations.literal: He had fine strategy; following the pacification of Zhongshan he was granted the marquisate of Pucheng and made Administrator of Pinglu, received exceptional favor, was given drums, pipes, and feather banners, and treated with ritual equal to a great provincial lord.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in strategy, he followed the pacification of Zhongshan, was made Marquis of Pucheng and administrator of Pinglu, and received drums, pipes, and banners with honors equal to a great lord.

sentences.zh: 莅政以威信著稱。

translations.literal: In governing his post he was famed for authority and trust.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was famed for authority and trust.

sentences.zh: 居官七年，乃以元易干代顗為郡。

translations.literal: After seven years in office Yuan Yigan was sent to replace Yi in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years Yuan Yigan was sent to replace him.

sentences.zh: 時易干子萬言得寵於太祖，易干恃其子，輕忽於顗，不告其狀，輕騎卒至，排顗墜牀而據顗坐。

translations.literal: At that time Yigan's son Wanyan had won Taizu's favor; Yigan relied on his son, slighted Yi, did not announce his arrival, and came with light cavalry that suddenly arrived, pushed Yi off the couch, and took Yi's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Yigan's son Wanyan had Taizu's favor; Yigan slighted Yi, gave no notice, arrived with light cavalry, pushed Yi from the couch, and took his seat.

sentences.zh: 顗不知代己，謂以罪見捕，既而知之，耻其侮慢，謂易干曰：「我更滿被代，常也；

translations.literal: Yi did not know he was being replaced and thought he was seized for a crime; once he knew, he was shamed by the insult and said to Yigan, "When my term is full and I am replaced—that is normal;
translations.idiomatic: Yi thought himself arrested for crime; learning the truth, he was shamed and said to Yigan, "When my term ends and I am replaced—that is normal;

sentences.zh: 汝無禮見辱，豈可容哉！

translations.literal: your rude insult—how can it be borne!"
translations.idiomatic: your rude insult—how can it be borne!"

sentences.zh: 」遂搏而殺之，以狀具聞。

translations.literal: " He then grappled and killed him and reported the full circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He grappled with him and killed him, then reported all to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖壯之。

translations.literal: Taizu admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu admired his act.

sentences.zh: 萬言累以訴請，乃詔顗輸贖。

translations.literal: Wanyan repeatedly appealed; an edict then ordered Yi to pay ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan appealed repeatedly; an edict ordered Yi to pay ransom.

sentences.zh: 顗乃自請罪，太祖赦之，復免其贖。

translations.literal: Yi then asked punishment for himself; Taizu pardoned him and again waived the ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Yi asked punishment for himself; Taizu pardoned him and waived the ransom.

sentences.zh: 病卒。

translations.literal: He died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness.

sentences.zh: 毗陵王順，昭成子地干之子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Piling Shun was a son of Diggan, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shun, Prince of Piling, was son of Diggan, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 性疏佷。

translations.literal: His nature was loose and obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: He was loose and obstinate by nature.

sentences.zh: 登國初，賜爵南安公。

translations.literal: At the start of Dengguo he was granted the title Duke of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Dengguo he was made Duke of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 及太祖討中山，留順守京師。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched on Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 栢肆之敗，軍人有亡歸者，言大軍奔散，不知太祖所在。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Baixi, soldiers who had fled back said the great army had scattered in flight and no one knew where Taizu was.
translations.idiomatic: After defeat at Baixi, fugitive soldiers said the main army had scattered and no one knew where Taizu was.

sentences.zh: 順聞之，欲自立，納莫題諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Shun heard this and wished to set himself up; Mo Ti remonstrated and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shun heard and meant to declare himself ruler; Mo Ti dissuaded him.

sentences.zh: 時賀力眷等聚眾作亂於陰館，順討之不克，乃從留宮自白登南入繁畤故城，阻灅水為固，以寧人心。

translations.literal: At that time Helijuan and others gathered a host and rebelled at Yin Guan; Shun attacked but could not overcome them, then left the palace, went south from Baideng into the old city of Fanchi, and blocked the Zhaishui as a defense to steady hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Helijuan rebelled at Yin Guan; Shun failed to suppress him, left the palace, entered old Fanchi south from Baideng, and held the Zhaishui to steady hearts.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，進封為王，位司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Taizu approved this, advanced his enfeoffment to prince, and made him Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved, raised him to prince, and made him colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 太祖好黃老，數召諸王及朝臣親為說之，在坐莫不祗肅，順獨坐寐欠伸，不顧而唾。

translations.literal: Taizu loved Huang-Lao doctrine and often summoned princes and court ministers to expound it in person; those seated none failed to be reverent—Shun alone sat dozing, stretched, paid no heed, and spat.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu loved Huang-Lao and lectured princes and ministers in person; all sat in reverence—Shun alone dozed, stretched, and spat.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，廢之。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and deposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and deposed him.

sentences.zh: 以王薨於家。

translations.literal: He died at home as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home, still a prince.

sentences.zh: 遼西公意烈，昭成子力真之子也。

translations.literal: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie was a son of Lizhen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie, Duke of Liaoxi, was son of Lizhen, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 先沒於慕容垂，太祖征中山，棄妻子迎於井陘。

translations.literal: He had earlier been lost to Murong Chui; when Taizu campaigned on Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children and came to welcome him at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: He had been lost to Murong Chui; when Taizu marched on Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children and welcomed him at Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 及平中原，有戰獲勳，賜爵遼西公，除廣平太守。

translations.literal: When the central plains were pacified he had merit in battle and capture; he was granted Duke of Liaoxi and made Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When the central plains were pacified he won merit in battle and was made Duke of Liaoxi and administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 時和跋為鄴行臺，意烈性雄耿，自以帝屬，耻居跋下，遂陰結徒黨，將襲鄴，發覺賜死。

translations.literal: At that time Heba was Mobile Court Commissioner at Ye; Yilie was bold and upright by nature, considered himself imperial kin, and was shamed to stand below Heba; he secretly gathered a faction and was about to raid Ye—discovered and ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: Heba held the mobile court at Ye; Yilie, bold and of imperial blood, was shamed to serve under him, plotted to seize Ye, was discovered, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 子拔干，博知古今。

translations.literal: His son Bagan was broadly learned in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bagan was learned in past and present.

sentences.zh: 父雖有罪，太祖以拔干宗親，委之心腹。

translations.literal: Though the father had guilt, Taizu, because Bagan was clan kin, entrusted him as a trusted intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Though the father was guilty, Taizu trusted Bagan as kin.

sentences.zh: 有計略，屢效忠勤。

translations.literal: He had stratagems and repeatedly showed loyal diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He had stratagems and served loyally again and again.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐阼，除勃海太守，吏人樂之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong took the throne he was made Administrator of Bohai; officials and people were glad.
translations.idiomatic: At Taizong's accession he became administrator of Bohai; officials and people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 賜爵武遂子。

translations.literal: He was granted the marquisate of Wusui.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Marquis of Wusui.

sentences.zh: 轉平原鎮將，得將士心。

translations.literal: Transferred to Commander of Pingyuan Garrison, he won officers' and soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to commander of Pingyuan Garrison, he won the troops' hearts.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰靈公。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Duke Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously styled Duke Ling.

sentences.zh: 子受洛，襲，進爵武邑公。

translations.literal: His son Shouluo inherited and was advanced to Duke of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouluo inherited and was advanced to Duke of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子叱奴，武川鎮將。

translations.literal: His son Chinu was Commander of Wuchuan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chinu commanded Wuchuan Garrison.

sentences.zh: 叱奴子洪超，頗有學涉。

translations.literal: Chinu's son Hongchao had considerable learning.
translations.idiomatic: Chinu's son Hongchao was widely learned.

sentences.zh: 大乘賊亂之後，詔洪超持節兼黃門侍郎綏慰冀部。

translations.literal: After the Dacheng bandit turmoil an edict made Hongchao Bearer of the Staff and concurrent Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate to soothe and comfort Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the Dacheng rebellion Hongchao was sent with credentials as attendant at the Yellow Gate to soothe Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 還，上言：「冀土寬廣，界去州六七百里，負海險遠，宜分置一州，鎮遏海曲。

translations.literal: On return he submitted: "Jizhou's land is broad; its borders lie six or seven hundred li from the provincial seat; it backs on the sea, dangerous and remote—a separate province should be set to guard the coast."
translations.idiomatic: On return he wrote: "Jizhou is vast; its borders lie six or seven hundred li from the seat; it backs on a dangerous coast—a separate province should guard the shore."

sentences.zh: 」朝議從之，後遂立滄州。

translations.literal: " Court discussion followed this; later Cangzhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed; Cangzhou was later established.

sentences.zh: 卒於北軍將、[14]光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He died while Northern Army General [14] and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He died as northern army general [14] and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 意烈弟勃，善射御，以勳賜爵彭城公。

translations.literal: Yilie's younger brother Bo was skilled at archery and charioteering; for merit he was granted Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie's brother Bo was skilled at archery and driving; for merit he was made Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 長子粟，襲。

translations.literal: His eldest son Su inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Su inherited.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，督諸軍屯漠南。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shizu's time he directed the armies stationed on the southern desert.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shizu he directed armies stationed on the southern desert.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕

translations.literal: The Rouran
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran

translations.literal: 〈lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈lacuna〉

sentences.zh: 表聞。

translations.literal: memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: and reported it in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 粟亮直，善馭眾，撫恤將士，必與之同勞逸。

translations.literal: Su was bright and upright, good at commanding the multitude; in comforting officers and soldiers he always shared their toil and rest.
translations.idiomatic: Su was upright and skilled at command; he shared toil and rest with his men.

sentences.zh: 征和龍，以功進封為王。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Helong he was advanced to prince for merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Helong campaign he was raised to prince for merit.

sentences.zh: 薨，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was buried with honor at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 粟弟渾，少善弓馬，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Hun from youth was skilled at bow and horse; Emperor Shizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Su's brother Hun was skilled with bow and horse from youth; Shizu praised him.

sentences.zh: 會有諸方使命，渾射獸三頭，發皆中之，舉坐咸以為善。

translations.literal: When envoys came from all quarters Hun shot three beasts—every arrow struck—and all seated thought it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys from many regions came, Hun shot three beasts, every arrow true, and all at table admired him.

sentences.zh: 及為宰官尚書，頗以驕縱為失，坐事免。

translations.literal: When he became Master of Writing for Palace Affairs he was rather proud and unrestrained in fault; for an offense he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: As master of writing for palace affairs he grew proud and unrestrained and was dismissed for an offense.

sentences.zh: 徙長社，為人所害。

translations.literal: He was moved to Changshe and was killed by someone.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Changshe and murdered.

sentences.zh: 昭成子窟咄。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng's son Kuduo.
translations.idiomatic: Kuduo, son of Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 昭成崩後，苻洛以其年長，逼徙長安，苻堅禮之，教以書學。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhaocheng died, Fu Luo, because he was older, forced him to move to Chang'an; Fu Jian treated him with ritual and taught him letters and learning.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhaocheng died, Fu Luo forced him to Chang'an for his seniority; Fu Jian honored him and taught him letters.

sentences.zh: 因亂隨慕容永東遷，永以為新興太守。

translations.literal: In the turmoil he followed Murong Yong east and Yong made him Administrator of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil he followed Murong Yong east; Yong made him administrator of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 劉顯之敗，遣弟亢埿等迎窟咄，遂逼南界，於是諸部騷動。

translations.literal: After Liu Xian's defeat he sent his younger brothers Kangqi and others to welcome Kuduo; Kuduo then pressed the southern border and all tribes were stirred.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Xian's defeat his brothers Kangqi and others welcomed Kuduo; he pressed the southern border and tribes stirred.

sentences.zh: 太祖左右于桓等謀應之，同謀人單烏干以告。

translations.literal: Taizu's attendants Yu Huan and others plotted to respond; a co-conspirator, Shan Wugan, reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu's attendant Yu Huan and others plotted to join him; Shan Wugan reported it.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮駭人心，沉吟未發。

translations.literal: Taizu feared alarming hearts and hesitated without acting.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu feared panic and hesitated.

sentences.zh: 後三日，桓以謀白其舅穆崇，崇又告之。

translations.literal: Three days later Huan told his uncle Mu Chong of the plot; Chong again reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Huan told his uncle Mu Chong; Chong reported again.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃誅桓等五人，餘莫題等七姓，悉原不問。

translations.literal: Taizu then executed Huan and five others; the seven surnames including Yu Mo Ti were all pardoned and not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu executed Huan and five others; seven clans including Yu Mo Ti were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 太祖慮內難，乃北踰陰山，幸賀蘭部，遣安同及長孫賀徵兵於慕容垂。

translations.literal: Taizu, fearing internal trouble, crossed north over the Yin Mountains, went in fortune to the Helan tribe, and sent An Tong and Changsun He to levy troops from Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing civil strife, Taizu crossed the Yin Mountains north to the Helan, and sent An Tong and Changsun He to levy troops from Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 賀亡奔窟咄，安同間行遂達中山。

translations.literal: He fled to Kuduo; An Tong by hidden routes reached Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He fled to Kuduo; An Tong by hidden routes reached Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂遣子賀驎步騎六千以隨之。

translations.literal: Murong Chui sent his son Heluo with six thousand foot and horse to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent his son Heluo with six thousand foot and horse to follow.

sentences.zh: 安同與垂使人蘭紇俱還，達牛川，窟咄兄子意烈捍之。

translations.literal: An Tong returned with Chui's envoy Lan He, reached Niuchuan; Kuduo's nephew Yilie resisted.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong returned with Chui's envoy Lan He to Niuchuan; Kuduo's nephew Yilie resisted.

sentences.zh: 安同乃隱藏於商賈囊中，至暮乃入空井，得免，仍奔賀驎。

translations.literal: An Tong hid in a merchant's pack-saddle; at dusk he entered an empty well, escaped, and ran to Heluo.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong hid in a merchant's pack; at dusk he entered an empty well, escaped, and fled to Heluo.

sentences.zh: 軍既不至，而稍前逼。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived but the enemy pressed forward little by little.
translations.idiomatic: The army had not arrived but the enemy pressed closer.

sentences.zh: 賀染干陰懷異端，乃為窟咄來侵北部。

translations.literal: Heranigan secretly harbored a separate design and came for Kuduo to invade the northern districts.
translations.idiomatic: Heranigan secretly turned traitor and invaded the north for Kuduo.

sentences.zh: 人皆驚駭，莫有固志。

translations.literal: All were alarmed; none had a firm will.
translations.idiomatic: All were terrified; none held firm.

sentences.zh: 於是北部大人叔孫普洛節及諸烏丸亡奔衞辰。

translations.literal: Then the northern great chief Shusun Puluo Jie and various Wuhuan fled to Wei Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The northern great chief Shusun Puluo Jie and Wuhuan fled to Wei Chen.

sentences.zh: 賀驎聞之，遽遣安同、朱譚等來。

translations.literal: Heluo heard this and urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo heard and urgently sent An Tong, Zhu Tan, and others.

sentences.zh: 既知賀驎軍近，眾乃小定。

translations.literal: Once they knew Heluo's army was near, the host was somewhat steadied.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heluo's army was known to be near, hearts steadied somewhat.

sentences.zh: 太祖自弩山幸牛川。

translations.literal: Taizu went from Nushan in fortune to Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu went from Nushan to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 窟咄進屯高柳。

translations.literal: Kuduo advanced and encamped at Gaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: Kuduo advanced and encamped at Gaoliu.

sentences.zh: 太祖復使安同詣賀驎，因克會期。

translations.literal: Taizu again sent An Tong to Heluo and fixed a date to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu again sent An Tong to Heluo and fixed a rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 安同還，太祖踰參合，出代北與賀驎會於高柳。

translations.literal: An Tong returned; Taizu crossed Canhe, came out from north of Dai, and met Heluo at Gaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: An Tong returned; Taizu crossed Canhe, came out from north of Dai, and met Heluo at Gaoliu.

sentences.zh: 窟咄困迫，望旗奔走，遂為衞辰殺之，帝悉收其眾。

translations.literal: Kuduo, hard pressed, fled at sight of the banners and was then killed by Wei Chen; the emperor gathered all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Kuduo fled at sight of the banners; Wei Chen killed him; the emperor gathered all his followers.

sentences.zh: 賀驎別帝，歸於中山。

translations.literal: Heluo took leave of the emperor and returned to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo took leave and returned to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Textual collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷十五 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」，百衲本、南本、汲本、局本有宋人校語云：「魏收書昭成子孫列傳亡。

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 15: in all editions' tables of contents this scroll is marked "deficient"; the Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions have Song scholars' collation notes saying, "Wei Shou's book, the collective biography of Emperor Zhaocheng's descendants, is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei juan 15: every edition's table of contents marks this scroll deficient; Song collation notes in the Baipu, Nan, Ji, and Ju editions say Wei Shou's biography of Zhaocheng's descendants is lost.

sentences.zh: 」殿本考證云：「魏收書亡，後人所補。

translations.literal: " The Palace edition's textual evidence says, "Wei Shou's book is lost; later persons supplemented it."
translations.idiomatic: The Palace edition's textual evidence says Wei Shou's text is lost and later hands supplemented it.

sentences.zh: 」按此卷亦是以北史卷一五魏宗室傳相同諸傳補，間有溢出字句，當出於高氏小史。

translations.literal: " Commentary: This juan too was supplemented from the corresponding biographies in Beishi juan 15, Imperial Clan of Wei; occasionally there are superfluous words and sentences that must come from the Gaoshi xiaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Note: This scroll was likewise patched from the parallel lives in Beishi juan 15 (Wei imperial clan); stray phrases now and then surely come from Gaoshi xiaoshi.

sentences.zh: 建國十年卒 北史卷一五魏宗室傳「十」年作「十五年」。

translations.literal: Died in the tenth year of Jianguo. Beishi juan 15, Imperial Clan of Wei, writes the "ten" of "ten years" as "fifteen years."
translations.idiomatic: "Died Jianguo year 10": Beishi juan 15 (Wei imperial clan) reads "ten years" as "fifteen years."

sentences.zh: 按卷一三皇后傳稱昭成皇后慕容氏「生獻明帝及秦明王」。

translations.literal: Commentary: Juan 13, Biographies of Empresses, says Empress Zhaocheng, née Murong, "gave birth to Emperor Xianming and the Prince of Qinming."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Juan 13 (Empresses) says Murong, empress of Zhaocheng, bore Emperor Xianming and the Prince of Qinming.

sentences.zh: 據卷一序紀，建國七年夏六月慕容氏才與什翼犍婚，而且翰還有兄寔，則建國十年，翰是否已出生尚不可知，即十五年死也至多是六七歲的小兒，與傳所云「年十五便請率騎征討」，「及長統兵」等語不符。

translations.literal: According to juan 1, Chronological Annals, in the sixth month, summer, of Jianguo year 7, Murong married Shiyijian, and moreover Han had an elder brother Shi; then in Jianguo year 10 whether Han had yet been born is still unknown—even death in year 15 would make him at most a child of six or seven, inconsistent with the biography's "at fifteen he requested to lead cavalry on campaign" and "when grown he commanded troops" and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 1's annals place Murong's marriage to Shiyijian in summer, sixth month, year 7 of Jianguo, and Han had an elder brother Shi; by year 10 his birth is uncertain, and even death in year 15 would leave him six or seven—far too young for "at fifteen he asked to lead horse on campaign" and "when grown he commanded armies."

sentences.zh: 此傳稱「建國十年卒」，北史稱「十五年卒」皆誤。

translations.literal: This biography says "died in Jianguo year 10," and Beishi says "died in year 15"—both are wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Both this life ('died year 10') and Beishi ('died year 15') are in error.

sentences.zh: 據卷一三獻明皇后賀氏傳稱「后少子秦王觚」，據此傳觚也是翰子，當是獻明太子拓跋寔死後，賀氏收繼為翰妻所生。

translations.literal: According to juan 13, Biography of Empress Xianming, née He, it says "the empress's younger son, Prince Gu of Qin"; according to this biography Gu was also Han's son—presumably after the Xianming Heir Apparent Tuoba Shi died, He adopted the children as born to Han's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 13 (Empress Xianming He) calls Gu the empress's younger son, Prince of Qin; this life makes Gu Han's son too—likely He adopted him after heir Tuoba Shi died, reckoning him Han's issue.

sentences.zh: 拓跋寔死在建國三十四年，見序紀，則翰死必在其後。

translations.literal: Tuoba Shi died in Jianguo year 34, as seen in the Chronological Annals; Han's death must therefore have come after that.
translations.idiomatic: Shi died in year 34 per the annals; Han cannot have died before that.

sentences.zh: 「十」字上下當有脫字。

translations.literal: Above and below the character "ten" there should be missing characters.
translations.idiomatic: Characters are missing before and after "ten."

sentences.zh: 乃祖受晉正朔 按儀不得自稱其祖為「乃祖」，「乃」字疑為「及」之訛。

translations.literal: His grandfather received the Jin calendar investiture. Commentary: By rites one may not call one's own grandfather "that grandfather"; the character "nai" is suspected to be a corruption of "ji" (and).
translations.idiomatic: "His grandfather received Jin investiture": one may not style one's forebear "that grandfather" by ritual; nai likely corrupts ji (and).

sentences.zh: 賜步挽几以優異之 冊府卷二七七

translations.literal: Granted a hand-drawn couch to treat him with especial favor. Cefu juan 277
translations.idiomatic: "Granted a hand-drawn couch to honor him specially." Cefu juan 277

sentences.zh: 〈三二六九〉

translations.idiomatic: folio 3269

sentences.zh: 頁「几」作「車」。

translations.literal: On the page "ji" (couch) is written "che" (cart).
translations.idiomatic: That folio reads che (cart) for ji (couch).

sentences.zh: 疑此傳「几」下脫「杖」字。

translations.literal: It is suspected that after "ji" in this biography the character "zhang" (staff) is missing.
translations.idiomatic: This life probably drops zhang (staff) after ji.

sentences.zh: 冊府以不可通，改「几」為「車」。

translations.literal: Cefu, because it would not parse, changed "ji" to "che."
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, finding the line unusable, emended ji to che.

sentences.zh: 領勃海之合口 按卷二太祖紀天興元年正月稱「略陽公元遵鎮勃海之合口」，這裏「領」當是「鎮」之訛。

translations.literal: Held Hegu's pass in Bohai. Commentary: Juan 2, Annals of Taizu, first month of Tianxing year 1 says "Yuanyang Duke Yuan Zun garrisoned Hegu's pass in Bohai"; here "ling" (to hold/lead) should be the corruption "zhen" (to garrison).
translations.idiomatic: "Held Hegu pass in Bohai": juan 2 (Taizu) has Yuan Zun "garrisoning" Hegu in the first month, Tianxing 1; ling should be zhen (garrison).

sentences.zh: 高祖將為齊郡王簡舉哀 諸本及北史卷一五常山王遵傳「簡」並作「蘭」。

translations.literal: Gaozu was about to mourn for Prince Jian of Qi commandery. In all editions and Beishi juan 15, Biography of Changshan Prince Zun, "Jian" is all written "Lan."
translations.idiomatic: "Gaozu was to mourn Prince Jian of Qi": every edition and Beishi juan 15 (Changshan Prince Zun) write Jian as Lan.

sentences.zh: 按本書卷二０、北史卷一九有齊郡王簡傳。

translations.literal: Commentary: This book juan 20 and Beishi juan 19 have biographies of Prince Jian of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Note: This work juan 20 and Beishi juan 19 both carry lives of Prince Jian of Qi.

sentences.zh: 其人死於太和二十三年，元宏已病，為之「力疾發哀」。

translations.literal: That person died in Taihe year 23; Yuan Hong was already ill and for him "forced himself while ill to perform mourning."
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe 23; Yuan Hong was already sick and "forced mourning despite illness."

sentences.zh: 本書高祖紀屢見，都作「簡」。

translations.literal: This book's Annals of Gaozu repeatedly mention him, all as "Jian."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's annals in this book always read Jian.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，故亦承北史之訛，今據紀及本傳改。

translations.literal: This biography was supplemented from Beishi, so it also inherits Beishi's error; now corrected according to the annals and the original biography.
translations.idiomatic: Patched from Beishi, this life repeats Beishi's mistake; emended per the annals and the dedicated biography.

sentences.zh: 仗入省 按「仗入省」不可解。

translations.literal: "Entered the Directorate with weapons." Commentary: "entered the Directorate with weapons" cannot be parsed.
translations.idiomatic: "Entered the Directorate with arms": the phrase will not parse.

sentences.zh: 北史卷六齊本紀上稱「孫騰帶仗入省，擅殺御史」。

translations.literal: Beishi juan 6, Basic Annals of Qi, Upper, says "Sun Teng entered the Directorate with belt and weapons and on his own authority killed a censor."
translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 6 (Qi annals, upper) has Sun Teng "entering the Directorate armed and killing a censor on his own authority."

sentences.zh: 知「仗」上當脫「帶」字。

translations.literal: One knows that above "zhan" (weapons) the character "dai" (bearing arms) should be missing.
translations.idiomatic: Dai (bearing arms) must be missing before zhan.

sentences.zh: 盛弟壽興 北史卷一五同，通志卷八四本傳作盛弟秉，字壽興」。

translations.literal: Sheng's younger brother Shouxing. Beishi juan 15 is the same; Tongzhi juan 84, this biography, makes it Sheng's younger brother Bing, courtesy name Shouxing."
translations.idiomatic: "Sheng's younger brother Shouxing": Beishi juan 15 agrees; Tongzhi juan 84 has Sheng's younger brother Bing, styled Shouxing."

sentences.zh: 以下此傳和北史作「壽興」處，通志都作「秉」。

translations.literal: Below, wherever this biography and Beishi read "Shouxing," Tongzhi all reads "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: Every later "Shouxing" in this life and Beishi appears as "Bing" in Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 下文壽興臨死自作墓誌云：「洛陽男子，姓元名景。

translations.literal: Below, on his deathbed Shouxing wrote his own epitaph saying: "A man of Luoyang, surname Yuan, personal name Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Below, Shouxing's deathbed self-composed epitaph runs: "A Luoyang man, family Yuan, personal name Jing."

sentences.zh: 」通志「景」也作「秉」。

translations.literal: " Tongzhi also writes "Jing" as "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: " Tongzhi likewise gives Bing for Jing.

sentences.zh: 按墓誌集釋元智墓誌

translations.literal: Commentary: Muzhi jishi, Epitaph of Yuan Zhi
translations.idiomatic: Note: Muzhi jishi, Epitaph of Yuan Zhi

sentences.zh: 〈圖版五一〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 51〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 51

sentences.zh: 稱「祖昺，使持節散騎常侍、都督徐州諸軍事、平東將軍、徐州刺史、宗正卿」。

translations.literal: states "grandfather Bing, Bearer of the Staff, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavaliers, Commander of All Military Affairs in Xuzhou, General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Xuzhou, Director of the Imperial Clan."
translations.idiomatic: names "Grandfather Bing, credential-bearing, Regular Cavalier Attendant, Commander of Xuzhou armies, General Pacifying the East, Xuzhou inspector, Director of the Imperial Clan."

sentences.zh: 前人據官銜和世系證「昺」即「壽興」。

translations.literal: Earlier scholars by official title and genealogy proved that "Bing" is "Shouxing."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier scholars identified Bing with Shouxing from titles and pedigree.

sentences.zh: 又卷六六崔亮傳也說他所劾的徐州刺史叫「元昞」。

translations.literal: Moreover juan 66, Biography of Cui Liang, also says the Xuzhou inspector he impeached was called "Yuan Bing."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 66 (Cui Liang) likewise names the Xuzhou inspector he impeached Yuan Bing.

sentences.zh: 壽興名「昞」

translations.literal: Shouxing's personal name was "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing's true name was Bing.

sentences.zh: 〈同昺〉

translations.literal: 〈same as Bing〉
translations.idiomatic: same graph as Bing

sentences.zh: 無可疑，北史避唐諱稱字，而自作墓誌則因有韵，改「昞」為「景」。

translations.literal: There is no doubt; Beishi uses the courtesy name to avoid Tang taboo, while in the self-composed epitaph, for rhyme's sake, "Bing" was changed to "Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond doubt: Beishi gives the style to dodge Tang taboo; the self-written epitaph rhymes Bing as Jing.

sentences.zh: 當時人地名常用同音字，或有他書作「秉」，鄭椎據以回改。

translations.literal: Personal and place names of the time often used homophonous characters; some other books write Bing, and Zheng Qiao reverted the text accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Homophones were common in names; some texts read the name as Bing, and Zheng Qiao restored that reading.

sentences.zh: 魏書原文，據崔亮傳自當作「昞」。

translations.literal: In the original Wei shu, according to the Cui Liang biography it ought to read "Bing."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou's original, per Cui Liang, should read Bing.

sentences.zh: 懸門發斷嶷要

translations.literal: The hanging gate snapped and struck Ning at the waist
translations.idiomatic: The gate mechanism broke and hit Ning's waist

translations.literal: 〈lacuna〉
translations.idiomatic: text missing

translations.idiomatic: "and emerged." Qian Daxin, Kaoyi juan 38: "Text is missing after yao; yao likely continues as

translations.literal: 〈i.e., waist〉
translations.idiomatic: waist (yao)

sentences.zh: 帶之類。」

translations.literal: belt and the like."
translations.idiomatic: belt or similar."

sentences.zh: 忠子暉 北史卷一五作「悝弟暉」，則是忠弟德之子。

translations.literal: Zhong's son Hui. Beishi juan 15 reads "Kui's younger brother Hui," making him the son of Zhong's younger brother De.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhong's son Hui": Beishi juan 15 has "Kui's younger brother Hui," hence De's son, not Zhong's.

sentences.zh: 按上文壽興傳稱「從兄暉」。

translations.literal: Commentary: In the Shouxing biography above it says "cousin Hui."
translations.idiomatic: Note: Shouxing's life above calls Hui a "cousin."

sentences.zh: 壽興是忠子，暉若也是忠子，豈能稱從兄？

translations.literal: Shouxing was Zhong's son; if Hui were also Zhong's son, how could he be called "cousin"?
translations.idiomatic: Shouxing is Zhong's son; if Hui were too, "cousin" would be impossible.

sentences.zh: 又附傳照例各從其父兄，暉傳不列於忠傳後，而列於德傳後，也可證他是德之子。

translations.literal: Moreover appended biographies by custom each follow their father or elder brother; Hui's biography is not placed after Zhong's biography but after De's biography—also proving he was De's son.
translations.idiomatic: Supplement lives follow their paternal line; Hui's is filed after De's, not Zhong's—more proof he is De's son.

sentences.zh: 宋趙明誠金石錄卷二十一元暉碑跋，已云魏書和北史不同，「以碑考之，北史是也」。

translations.literal: Song Zhao Mingcheng, Jinshi lu juan 21, colophon to the stele of Yuan Hui, already said Wei shu and Beishi differ, "examining by the stele, Beishi is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Mingcheng (Song), Jinshi lu juan 21, on Yuan Hui's stele already noted Wei shu disagrees with Beishi and concluded: "The stele proves Beishi right."

sentences.zh: 墓誌集釋元暉墓誌

translations.literal: Muzhi jishi, Epitaph of Yuan Hui
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui's epitaph in Muzhi jishi

sentences.zh: 〈圖版五五〉

translations.literal: 〈plate 55〉
translations.idiomatic: plate 55

sentences.zh: 稱「父冀州刺史、河間簡公」。

translations.literal: states "father, Inspector of Jizhou, Duke Jian of Hejian."
translations.idiomatic: calls his father "Jizhou inspector, Duke Jian of Hejian."

sentences.zh: 集釋卷三據元侔、元峻、元愔墓誌

translations.literal: Jishi juan 3, according to the epitaphs of Yuan Mou, Yuan Jun, and Yuan Yin
translations.idiomatic: Jishi juan 3, citing epitaphs of Yuan Mou, Yuan Jun, and Yuan Yin

sentences.zh: 〈均見本書〉

translations.literal: 〈all seen in this book〉
translations.idiomatic: all cited in this work

sentences.zh: ，證明此「河間簡公」即此傳的元德，元侔等誌的元於德，北史是而魏書非。

translations.literal: , proves that this "Duke Jian of Hejian" is Yuan De of this biography; Yuan Mou and the others' epitaphs have Yuan as son of De—Beishi is right and Wei shu is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: , shows "Duke Jian of Hejian" is the Yuan De of this life; Mou and the others name Yuan as De's son—Beishi correct, Wei shu not.

translations.literal: In all two hundred seventy juan. Zhang Senkai says: "Suishu Jingji zhi
translations.idiomatic: "Two hundred seventy scrolls in all." Zhang Senkai: "Suishu, Bibliographic Treatise

translations.literal: 〈juan 34〉
translations.idiomatic: juan 34

sentences.zh: 只七十卷。」

translations.literal: has only seventy juan."
translations.idiomatic: lists only seventy scrolls."

sentences.zh: 神龜元年卒 按元暉墓誌：「神龜二年九月庚午卒。

translations.literal: Died in Shengui year 1. Commentary: Yuan Hui's epitaph: "died on gengwu, ninth month, Shengui year 2.
translations.idiomatic: "Died Shengui 1": Yuan Hui's epitaph gives "died gengwu, ninth month, Shengui 2."

sentences.zh: 」此傳誤。

translations.literal: " This biography is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: " The life is wrong.

sentences.zh: 卒於北軍將 「北軍將」，無此官名。

translations.literal: Died while North Army General. "North Army General"—there is no such office title.
translations.idiomatic: "Died as North Army General": no such office exists.

sentences.zh: 「北」上當脫一字，「將軍」誤倒為「軍將」。

translations.literal: Above "bei" (north) one character should be missing; "jiang jun" (general) was wrongly inverted to "jun jiang" (army general).
translations.idiomatic: A character is missing before bei; jiangjun was transposed to junjiang.
